⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr related to us, from Mis'ar ibn 'Abd al-Karim, from Musa ibn Abi Kathir, from Ibn 'Abbas, that it reached him that Umm Hani mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), on the day of the conquest of Makkah, prayed the forenoon prayer, eight rak'ahs. Ibn 'Abbas said: I had thought that this hour had a prayer. Allah says: ﴿they glorify [Him] at dusk and at sunrise﴾.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Abi Salama related to us, saying: Sadaqa related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah related to me, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Ayyub ibn Safwan, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, that Ibn 'Abbas did not pray the forenoon prayer. He said: I brought him to Umm Hani, and I said: Tell this one what you told me. Umm Hani said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon me in my house on the day of the conquest, and he ordered water to be poured into a bowl, then he ordered a cloth, which was held between me and him, and he washed, then he sprinkled a corner of the house and prayed eight rak'ahs, and that was the forenoon prayer, their standing, bowing, prostrating and sitting being equal, close to one another. Ibn 'Abbas went out saying: I have read what is between the two covers, and I did not know the forenoon prayer until now: ﴿they glorify [Him] at dusk and at sunrise﴾. I used to say: where is the prayer of ishraq? Then he said: after them is the prayer of ishraq.

⁕ 'Amr ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah related to us, from Mutawakkil, from Ayyub ibn Safwan, client of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, that Umm Hani bint Abi Talib narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon her on the day of the conquest, then he mentioned something similar.

And from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿they glorify [Him] at dusk﴾, the like of that.

* *

And His saying ﴿And the birds gathered﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We subjected the birds, glorifying with Him, gathered (mahshurah), meaning: assembled for Him. It is mentioned that when he (ﷺ) glorified, the mountains responded and the birds gathered to him, glorifying with him, and their gathering to him was their hashr. We have already mentioned the statements of those who interpret the Qur'an regarding the meaning of hashr earlier, so we disliked repeating it.

Qatada used to say in this place:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And the birds gathered﴾: subjected.

* *

And His saying ﴿all of them returning to Him﴾

He says: all of that is obedient to Him, returning to His obedience and command. By "all" he means: all the birds.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿all of them returning to Him﴾: that is, obedient.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And the birds gathered, all of them returning to Him﴾, he said: all of them are obedient to Him.

Others said: the meaning is: all of them are glorifying Allah.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿And the birds gathered, all of them returning to Him﴾, he says: glorifying Allah.

* *

And His saying ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom﴾

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning by which his kingdom was strengthened. Some said: it was strengthened by soldiers and men; he was guarded every day and night by four thousand, four thousand.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom﴾, he said: he was guarded every day and night by four thousand, four thousand.

Others said: what strengthened his kingdom was that he was given awe from people because of a judgment he had passed.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Harb related to me, saying: Musa related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from 'Alba' ibn Ahmar, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man from the Children of Israel sought redress against a man of their nobles, and the two gathered before Dawud the Prophet (ﷺ). The complainant said: This one seized my cows from me. Dawud asked the man about that, and he denied it. Then he asked the other for evidence, and he had no evidence. Dawud said to them both: Stand until I consider your matter. So they left his presence. Then Allah revealed to Dawud in a dream that he should kill the man against whom redress was sought. He said: This is a vision, and I will not hasten until I am certain. Then Allah revealed to Dawud again in a dream that he should kill the man, and Allah revealed to him a third time that he should kill him, or the punishment from Allah would come to him. So Dawud sent to the man: Allah has revealed to me that I should kill you. The man said: You would kill me without evidence and without verification?! Dawud said to him: Yes, by Allah, I will surely carry out the command of Allah concerning you. When the man realized that he was going to kill him, he said: Do not hasten against me until I inform you. By Allah, I was not seized for this sin, but I had secretly killed this one's father, and for that I am being killed. So Dawud ordered him to be killed. Then the awe of the Children of Israel for Dawud increased at that time, and his kingdom was strengthened by it. This is the saying of Allah: ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom﴾.

The most correct of these statements, in our view, is to say: Allah, blessed and exalted, informed that He strengthened the kingdom of Dawud, and the text does not specify that this strengthening was by soldiers and armies alone, to the exclusion of the awe people had for him, nor the awe of people for him to the exclusion of the armies. It is possible that his strengthening was by some of what we have mentioned, and it is possible that it was by all of it. No statement is more correct regarding this than the word of Allah, since no report requiring submission has specified one of the meanings of strengthening.

* *

And His saying ﴿and gave him wisdom﴾

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of wisdom (al-hikmah) in this place. Some said: it refers to prophethood.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿and gave him wisdom﴾, he said: prophethood.

Others said: it means that he knew the sunnah.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and gave him wisdom﴾: that is, the sunnah.

We have already explained the meaning of wisdom in other places with its evidences, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it here.

* *

And His saying ﴿and decisive speech (fasl al-khitab)﴾

The interpreters differed regarding its meaning. Some said: it means that he was taught judgment and understanding of it.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And We gave him wisdom and decisive speech﴾, he said: he was given understanding.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿decisive speech﴾, he said: correctness in judgment and understanding of it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿decisive speech﴾, he said: the knowledge of judgment.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And We gave him wisdom and decisive speech﴾, he said: the disputes in which people dispute before him, that decisive speech is the speech of understanding, and correctness in judgment and evidences.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Husayn, who said: I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman say: fasl al-khitab is judgment.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: decisive speech, by requiring the claimant to produce evidence and the defendant to take an oath.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, saying: al-Sha'bi or another related to me, from Shurayh, that he said regarding His saying ﴿decisive speech﴾: the evidence of the claimant, or the oath of the defendant.

⁕ Yaqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, regarding His saying ﴿And We gave him wisdom and decisive speech﴾, he said: I was informed from Shurayh that he said: two witnesses or an oath.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Mu'tamir related to us, saying: I heard Dawud say: It reached me that Shurayh said: ﴿decisive speech﴾ is two witnesses for the claimant and an oath for the one who denies.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Tawus, that Shurayh said to a man: This one finds fault with me over what was given to Dawud: the witnesses and the oaths.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Shurayh, that he said regarding this verse ﴿decisive speech﴾: the witnesses and the oaths.

⁕ 'Imran ibn Musa related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His saying ﴿And We gave him wisdom and decisive speech﴾, he said: an oath or a witness.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿decisive speech﴾: the evidence upon the claimant and the oath upon the one claimed against; this is decisive speech.

Others said: rather, it is the saying "amma ba'd" (as for what follows).

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His saying ﴿decisive speech﴾, he said: a man's saying: "amma ba'd".

The most correct of these statements, in our view, is to say: Allah informed that He gave Dawud, may Allah's blessings be upon him, decisive speech. Al-fasl is cutting off, and al-khitab is address. Whoever cuts off one man's address to another, when one of them is judging between them, the judge cuts off the matter between the judge and his opponent with a correct ruling; and whoever cuts off his address to his companion by obliging the addressed party to what is due upon him in judgment, if he is the claimant, by establishing evidence for his claim, and if he is the defendant, by imposing the oath if his opponent requests it. And whoever cuts off address, which is a sermon at the end of one story and the beginning of another, separates them with "amma ba'd." Since all of that is possible under the apparent meaning of the report, and there is no indication in this verse as to which of these is intended, nor has any established report from the Messenger (ﷺ) been transmitted about it, the correct position is that the report is general, as Allah made it general, so it is said: Dawud was given decisive speech in judgment, in discourse, and in sermons.

**The interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He:** ﴿And has the news of the adversaries reached you, when they climbed over the wall of the prayer chamber? (21) When they entered upon David and he was alarmed by them, they said, "Do not fear. Two adversaries have wronged one another, so judge between us with truth, and do not exceed the bounds, and guide us to the even path." (22)﴾

He, Exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And has the news of the adversary reached you, O Muhammad?" It has been said that by "the adversary" in this place two angels are meant, and it is expressed in the singular form because it is a verbal noun (maṣdar), like *al-zūr* and *al-safar*, which is not made dual or plural. From this is the saying of Labid:

*"And an adversary who pursue vengeance-claims, as though they were / stallions in rut, every white-faced, unbroken camel."* [[The verse is by Labid (Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda, folio 213b). He said: "*Naba' al-khasm*" applies to the singular and the plural. Labid said: "*Wa khasm...*" (the verse). *Al-dhuhul* is the plural of *dhahl*, meaning vengeance. *Al-qurum* is the plural of *qarm*, the great stallion of camels. *Ghayārā* is the plural of *ghayrān*. *Al-azhar* is the white one. *Al-muṣ'ab* is the strong, powerful one who is held back from riding and work because of his stallion-like vigour (Lisan al-'Arab, s.v. ṣ-‘-b). He likened the powerful adversaries to stallions of camels.]]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿when they climbed over the wall of the prayer chamber﴾: he says they entered upon him from other than the door of the prayer chamber. The *miḥrab* (prayer chamber) is the front and the most noble part of every assembly and house.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿when they entered upon David﴾:

He repeated *idh* (when) twice. Some of the grammarians said concerning this: their meaning may be like a single one, as when you say, "I struck you when you entered upon me, when you became bold," so that the entering is the emboldening. Or you may make one of them carry the sense of *lammā* (when/as soon as), so that it is as if he said, "when they climbed over the chamber, *lammā* they entered." He said: If you wish, you may make *lammā* apply to the first. When *lammā* comes first or last, it follows its counterpart, as you say, "I gave him when he asked me," where the asking is before the giving in its precedence and in its sequence.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿so he was alarmed by them﴾:

Someone might say: what was the reason for his alarm at them, when they were two adversaries? His alarm at them was because they had entered upon him from other than the door by which entry to him was made, so their entering in this manner startled him. It has also been said that his alarm was from them because they entered upon him at night, at a time when he was not sitting to judge between people. They said, ﴿Do not fear﴾: He, Exalted is His remembrance, says: the adversary said to him, "Do not fear, O David," because they saw that he had been startled by their entering upon him from other than the door. In the speech there is an omitted element, which is understood from what is expressed, namely: "the matter for which we seek a judgement is two adversaries" (i.e., "we are"). The omission of its expression is permissible, although the two adversaries need the one who will judge, because His saying ﴿two adversaries﴾ is an act of the speaker. The Arabs omit, for the speaker and the one addressed (the speaker and the listener), that which governs their verbs, and they hardly do this with anyone else. They say to a man whom they address, "Are you departing, O so-and-so?", and the speaker says to his companion, "May you be well and kind to you." They do this only with the speaker and the one addressed, because both are present, and the hearer knows the speaker's intent when the noun is omitted. Most of this occurs in questions, though it is permissible outside questions too, as in, "Is a companion riding?" From this is His saying ﴿two adversaries﴾. And from it is the saying of the poet:

*"Say, when you have passed the land of 'Amir / and passed the two tribes of Nahd and Khash'am: / 'We are two of the Jarm ibn Rabban, for they / refused to bring grain in times of hardship.'"* [[These two verses are among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 278) to show that *khasmān* in His saying ﴿they said: two adversaries﴾ is in the nominative by an implied *naḥnu* (we). He said: The Arabs omit for the speaker and the addressee what governs their verb, and they hardly do so with anyone other than the addressee or the speaker. Among this is that you say to a man, "Are you going?" or the speaker says, "We join you, God willing, and do good to you." Among this is that you say to a man, "Are you going?" ... Because the speaker and the one addressed are present, the meaning of their names is known when they are left out. Most of it occurs in questions; they say, "Is he generous?" "Are you a speaker?", but it may also occur outside questions. So His saying "two adversaries" is of this kind. The poet said: "Say when ..." (the two verses). And it has come in reports of the Prophet's travellers' returning: "Penitent, returning, praising our Lord"... etc. I say: the evidence in the two verses is His saying "*nazi'ān*", meaning "we are *nazi'ān*". It is in the nominative by an implied element before it, even though it has no interrogative.]]

And the saying of another:

*"The daughter of al-Ka'bi says on the day I meet her, / 'Are you going forth with the army, or are you holding back?'"* [[This verse is also among the evidences of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, to show that the subject (mubtada') may be omitted, and this often occurs with an interrogative present in the speech, as in the verse: "Are you going forth with the army or are you holding back?", i.e., "are you going forth ...?"]]

From this is their saying, "*Muḥsinatan fa-hayli*" [a proverb], and the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "*Āʾibūna tāʾibūna*" (Returning, repenting). And his saying: "He will come on the Day of Resurrection with 'Despairing of God's mercy' written between his eyes." All of these are with a pronoun which is in the nominative.

As for His, Mighty and Majestic is He, saying ﴿one of us has wronged the other﴾: he says, one of us has transgressed against his companion without right. ﴿So judge between us with truth﴾: he says, decide between us with justice. ﴿And do not exceed the bounds﴾: he says, do not deviate, and do not be excessive in your judgement, by inclining towards one of us against the other. In it there are two dialects: *ashatta* and *shatta*. From *al-ishtāṭ* is the saying of al-Ahwas:

*"Oh people, my blamers have exceeded the bounds, / and they claim that my falsehood has destroyed my right."* [[This verse is by al-Ahwas, and like the previous one it is related in Lisan al-'Arab under *sh-t-ṭ*, and in Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda as evidence that the meaning of *ashatat* with a hamza at its beginning is "went far". *Awdā bi-ḥaqqihi*: took it away and destroyed it.]]

And it is heard from some of them: "You exceeded the bounds with me in the price (*sawm*)." As for distance, most of their speech is: "*shaṭṭat al-dār*" (the house was far), so it is "*tashiṭṭu*", as the poet said:

*"Tomorrow the dwelling of our neighbours will be far away, / and after tomorrow the dwelling is further still."* [[This verse is among the evidences of Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 213) at His saying ﴿and do not exceed the bounds﴾, meaning "do not be excessive." He recited "*tashiṭṭu ghadan dār jīrānanā*" (the verse). It is said: "*kallaftanī shaṭaṭan*" (you burdened me with excess), and "*shaṭṭat al-dār*": it was far. In Lisan al-'Arab (sh-t-ṭ): In the revelation: "and do not exceed the bounds." It has also been read with the first *ṭā'* vowelled with a *ḍamma* and the *tā'* with a *fatḥa*, meaning: "do not go far from the truth."]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾:

He says: guide us to the straight way's midpoint.

Those who interpret (ahl al-ta'wil, the exegetes) have said things similar to what we have said regarding His saying ﴿and do not exceed the bounds﴾.

Those who said this:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿and do not exceed the bounds﴾: that is, do not incline.
- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿and do not exceed the bounds﴾, he says: do not be unjust.
- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and do not exceed the bounds﴾: deviate from the truth.

And they have said similarly regarding His saying ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾:

Those who said this:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾: to His justice and His good.
- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾: to the justice of judgement.
- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾: to the truth, which is the truth: the straight path. ﴿And do not exceed the bounds﴾: do not go to other than it.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾: that is, bring us to the truth, and do not turn us aside from it to something else.

And the saying of another:

*"The daughter of al-Ka'bi says on the day I meet her, / 'Are you going forth with the army, or are you holding back?'"* [[This verse is also among the evidences of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, to show that the subject (mubtada') may be omitted, and this often occurs with an interrogative present in the speech, as in the verse: "Are you going forth with the army or are you holding back?", i.e., "are you going forth ...?"]]

From this is their saying, "*Muḥsinatan fa-hayli*" [a proverb], and the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "*Āʾibūna tāʾibūna*" (Returning, repenting). And his saying: "He will come on the Day of Resurrection with 'Despairing of God's mercy' written between his eyes." All of these are with a pronoun which is in the nominative.

As for His, Mighty and Majestic is He, saying ﴿one of us has wronged the other﴾: he says, one of us has transgressed against his companion without right. ﴿So judge between us with truth﴾: he says, decide between us with justice. ﴿And do not exceed the bounds﴾: he says, do not deviate, and do not be excessive in your judgement, by inclining towards one of us against the other. In it there are two dialects: *ashatta* and *shatta*. From *al-ishtāṭ* is the saying of al-Ahwas:

*"Oh people, my blamers have exceeded the bounds, / and they claim that my falsehood has destroyed my right."* [[This verse is by al-Ahwas, and like the previous one it is related in Lisan al-'Arab under *sh-t-ṭ*, and in Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda as evidence that the meaning of *ashatat* with a hamza at its beginning is "went far". *Awdā bi-ḥaqqihi*: took it away and destroyed it.]]

And it is heard from some of them: "You exceeded the bounds with me in the price (*sawm*)." As for distance, most of their speech is: "*shaṭṭat al-dār*" (the house was far), so it is "*tashiṭṭu*", as the poet said:

*"Tomorrow the dwelling of our neighbours will be far away, / and after tomorrow the dwelling is further still."* [[This verse is among the evidences of Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 213) at His saying ﴿and do not exceed the bounds﴾, meaning "do not be excessive." He recited "*tashiṭṭu ghadan dār jīrānanā*" (the verse). It is said: "*kallaftanī shaṭaṭan*" (you burdened me with excess), and "*shaṭṭat al-dār*": it was far. In Lisan al-'Arab (sh-t-ṭ): In the revelation: "and do not exceed the bounds." It has also been read with the first *ṭā'* vowelled with a *ḍamma* and the *tā'* with a *fatḥa*, meaning: "do not go far from the truth."]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾:

He says: guide us to the straight way's midpoint.

Those who interpret (ahl al-ta'wil, the exegetes) have said things similar to what we have said regarding His saying ﴿and do not exceed the bounds﴾.

Those who said this:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿and do not exceed the bounds﴾: that is, do not incline.
- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿and do not exceed the bounds﴾, he says: do not be unjust.
- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and do not exceed the bounds﴾: deviate from the truth.

And they have said similarly regarding His saying ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾:

Those who said this:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾: to His justice and His good.
- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾: to the justice of judgement.
- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾: to the truth, which is the truth: the straight path. ﴿And do not exceed the bounds﴾: do not go to other than it.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾: that is, bring us to the truth, and do not turn us aside from it to something else.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 23:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this is my brother. He has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe. So he said, "Entrust it to me," and he overcame me in speech.﴾

This is a parable that the two litigants, who climbed over the wall into David's prayer niche (mihrab), presented to him. It is said that David had, as was reported, ninety-nine wives, and the man whom he had sent to battle until he was killed had only one wife. When he was killed, David married his wife, as was mentioned. So one of them said to him: ﴿Indeed, this is my brother﴾, meaning: my brother in religion.

As for what was narrated:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿Indeed, this is my brother﴾: i.e., in my religion. ﴿He has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe﴾.

It is also mentioned that in the recitation of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) it reads: "Indeed, this is my brother. He has ninety-nine ewes, female (unthā)." This is by way of emphasis on the word, as the Arabs say "this is a male man (rajul dhakar)." They do not usually do this except with a feminine or masculine noun whose masculinity or femininity is inherent in itself, such as woman, man, and she-camel. They would not usually say "this is a female house (dār unthā)" or "a female wrap (milhafa unthā)," because its femininity is in its name and not in its meaning. It was also said: by his words "female (unthā)" he meant that she was beautiful.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ It was reported to me from al-Muharibi, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿Indeed, this is my brother. He has ninety-nine ewes, female﴾, meaning by her femininity, her beauty.

* *

As for His words ﴿So he said, "Entrust it to me"﴾:

He means: he said to me, "Give her up to me and place her under my care."

As for what was narrated:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Entrust it to me﴾: "Give it to me, divorce her for me, marry her, and leave her way."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿Entrust it to me﴾, i.e., carry me upon it.

* *

As for His words ﴿and he overcame me in speech﴾:

He means: he became mightier than me in his address to me, for if he spoke, he was more eloquent than me, and if he seized, he was stronger than me and overpowered me.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: Abdullah said regarding His words ﴿and he overcame me in speech﴾: "David did not go beyond saying: 'Give her up to me.'"

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from al-Mas'udi, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "He did not go beyond saying: 'Give her up to me.'"

⁕ Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi also narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, who said: Abdullah said: "David did not go beyond saying: ﴿Entrust it to me﴾."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿and he overcame me in speech﴾: "If I called, and he called, his call would be greater; and if I seized, and he seized, his seizing would be stronger than mine. That is His words ﴿and he overcame me in speech﴾."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and he overcame me in speech﴾: i.e., he wronged me and overpowered me.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿and he overcame me in speech﴾: "He overpowered me, and that is the 'izz (might); he said: and al-khitab (address) is speech."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding ﴿and he overcame me in speech﴾: i.e., he overpowered me in address, and he was stronger than me, so he took possession of my ewe in addition to his ewes, and left me with nothing.

⁕ It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and he overcame me in speech﴾: "If he spoke, he was more eloquent than me; if he seized, he was stronger than me; and if he called, his call was greater than mine."

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "He has certainly wronged you by asking for your ewe to be added to his ewes. Indeed, many partners wrong one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they." And David thought that We had tested him, so he asked his Lord for forgiveness, fell down bowing, and turned in repentance.﴾ (38:24)**

His exalted mention says: David said to the disputing claimant against his companion, "Your companion has certainly wronged you by asking for your ewe to be added to his ewes." This is one of the cases where the *ha'* (the pronoun suffix) has been dropped, so the noun is made genitive (*idafah*) to the object after the dropped *ha'*. Similar to it is His exalted words: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good﴾, meaning: of asking for it (*min du'a'ihi bil-khayr*). When the *ha'* was removed from *du'a'* it was made genitive to *al-khayr*, and the *ba'* was removed from *al-khayr*.

Here the ewe is used as a metaphor for the woman, as the Arabs do. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

*"I was its guide, and [I was] the sheep of a watchful one,
Wary, who narrows his eye to its neglect."*

[The verse is in the *diwan* of al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays (Cairo edition, p. 27), from his *lamiyyah* which begins: "Sumayyah departed at dawn with her camels..." The verse in it reads: "I spent the night..." in place of "I was," and the pronoun in *ra'idaha* refers to the earth which was adorned with kinds of plants in the previous verse. *Shah* ("sheep") is an animal used as a metaphor for a woman. *Muhadhir* means one who is very wary over her and constantly watches her, and he is her husband. His saying *shah* in the genitive is conjoined to his saying in a previous verse: "Many a seductress who cut off her union." He says: many a stricken one, a cloud, I spent the night guiding her, and many a woman who has a husband who is wary over her and watches her with intense vigilance, until he neglects her toward the end of the night, and I approached her... etc.]

What is meant by "the sheep" is the wife of a man whom people are wary over. What is meant is: "You have been wronged by asking for your one wife to be added to his ninety-nine wives."

\* \*

And His saying: ﴿And indeed many partners wrong one another﴾

He says: indeed many associates oppress one another ﴿except those who believe﴾ in God ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, meaning: they act in obedience to God and abide by His command and prohibition, and do not transgress them ﴿and few are they﴾. In His saying ﴿and few are they﴾ there are two possibilities for *ma* (the particle): The first is that it is a *silah* (an expletive/connecting particle) meaning "and few they are," so that its presence or absence does not corrupt the meaning of the statement. The second is that it is a noun, and *hum* (they) is its *silah*, meaning "and few are those you find," as one says: "I used to think you were more intelligent than you are," where *anta* ("you") is the *silah* of *ma*, and the meaning is: "I used to think your intelligence was greater than it is." So *ma* together with the noun forms a verbal noun (*masdar*). If you did not intend the verbal noun, the statement would be with *man* (who), because *man* is used for people and those like them. It is reported from the Arabs: "I used to see you as more intelligent than you are, similarly," and "I used to think that he was other than he is," meaning: "I used to see him as other than what I saw."

It has been related from Ibn Abbas regarding this:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and few are they﴾: he says: "and few are those who."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they﴾: "Few are those who do not oppress."

According to this interpretation which Ibn Abbas gave, the meaning of the statement is: "except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are those who are likewise, meaning those who do not oppress one another." And *ma*, according to this view, means *man* (who).

\* \*

And His saying: ﴿And David thought that We had tested him﴾

He says: David knew that We had tried him, as:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And David thought﴾: David knew.

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿And David thought that We had tested him﴾: he said: he thought that he had been tested with that.

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And David thought that We had tested him﴾: he said: he thought that he had been tried with that.

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And David thought that We had tested him﴾: he said: "We tested him."

The Arabs often direct *zann* (thought/supposition) when it is introduced upon a report to knowledge that comes not from direct observation.

\* \*

And His saying: ﴿So he asked his Lord for forgiveness﴾

He says: David asked his Lord for forgiveness for his sin. ﴿And fell down bowing﴾, he says: he fell down prostrating to God. ﴿And turned in repentance﴾, he says: he returned to the pleasure of his Lord and repented of his wrongdoing.

There has been disagreement about the cause of the trial with which the prophet of God, David (ﷺ), was tested. Some said: the cause of that was that he remembered what God had given Abraham, Isaac and Jacob of good praise that remains for them among people, so he wished for the like of it. It was said to him: "They were tested and they were patient," so he asked to be tested as they were tested, and to be given as they were given, if he were patient.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Has there reached you the report of the disputants, when they climbed over the sanctuary wall?﴾ He said: David said: "O Lord, You have given Abraham, Isaac and Jacob of the remembrance what I would have loved for You to give me the like of." God said: "I tested them with what I did not test you with. If you wish, I will test you with the like of what I tested them with, and give you as I gave them." He said: "Yes." He said to him: "Then act, until I see your trial." So it was what God willed it to be, and that lasted long for him, and he almost forgot it. Then while he was in his sanctuary, a dove of gold fell upon him, and he wanted to take it, so it flew to a window of the sanctuary, and he went to take it, and it flew away. So he looked out from the window and saw a woman bathing, and the prophet of God (ﷺ) came down from the sanctuary and sent for her, and she came to him. He asked her about her husband and her condition, and she informed him that her husband was absent. So he wrote to the commander of that expedition that he should appoint him over the expeditions, so that her husband would be destroyed. He did so, and his companions were struck while he was safe, and sometimes they were given victory. When God, mighty and majestic, saw what David had fallen into, He wished to rescue him. Then one day, while David was in his sanctuary, the two disputants climbed over the wall from the front of him. When he saw them, while he was reciting, he was frightened and fell silent, and said: "I have been made weak in my kingdom, so that people climb over my sanctuary against me." The two said to him: ﴿Do not fear. Two disputants, one of us has wronged the other. So judge between us with truth, and do not be unjust, and guide us to the even path﴾ and we had no choice but to come to you, so listen to us. One of them said: ﴿This brother of mine has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe, so he says, "Entrust her to me," and he overpowers me in speech﴾, meaning: he wants to complete a hundred with her and leave me with nothing. ﴿And he overpowers me in speech﴾: he said: if I call, he calls more, and if I strike, he strikes harder than I do. That is His saying ﴿and he overpowers me in speech﴾. David said to him: "You were more in need of your ewe than he is" ﴿He has certainly wronged you by asking for your ewe to be added to his ewes﴾ ... to His saying ﴿and few are they﴾. He forgot himself (ﷺ), and the two angels looked at each other when he said that, and one of them smiled at the other. David saw it, and he thought that he had been tested. ﴿So he asked his Lord for forgiveness, fell down bowing, and turned in repentance﴾ for forty nights, until green growth sprouted from the tears of his eyes. Then God strengthened his kingdom for him.

- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿Has there reached you the report of the disputants, when they climbed over the sanctuary wall?﴾ He said: David had divided time into three days: a day on which he judged between people, a day on which he was alone for the worship of his Lord, and a day on which he was alone with his wives. He had ninety-nine wives. And among what he read in the books was that he found in them the virtue of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. When he found that in what he read in the books, he said: "O Lord, all good has been taken by my forefathers who were before me. So give me the like of what You gave them, and do with me as You did with them." He said: God revealed to him: "Your forefathers were tested with trials with which you were not tested. Abraham was tested with the sacrifice of his son, Isaac was tested with the loss of his sight, and Jacob was tested with grief over Joseph, and you have not been tested with any of that." He said: "O Lord, test me with the like of what You tested them with, and give me the like of what You gave them." He said: then it was revealed to him: "You will indeed be tested, so be cautious." He said: then he remained after that as long as God willed him to remain, when Satan came in the form of a dove of gold, until it fell at his feet while he was standing praying. He stretched out his hand to take it, and it withdrew, and he followed it. It went far until it fell into a window, and he went to take it, and it flew out of the window. He looked to see where it would land, so that he could send after it. He saw a woman bathing on her roof, and he saw a woman of the most beautiful creation. The woman turned her glance and saw him, so she threw her hair over herself and covered herself with it. He said: that increased his desire for her. He asked about her, and was informed that she had a husband, and that her husband was absent at such and such a frontier post. He said: so he sent to the commander of the frontier post that he should send Uriah [[It will come in 149 that his name is "Uriah."]] to such and such an enemy. He said: so he sent him, and he conquered for him. He said: and he wrote to him with that. He said: then he wrote to him again: "Send him to such and such an enemy, who are more severe in might." He said: so they sent him, and he conquered for him as well. He said: so he wrote to David about that. He said: so he wrote to him: "Send him to such and such an enemy," so he sent him, and he was killed the third time. He said: and he married his wife.

He said: When she entered upon him, he said: she did not stay with him except briefly until God sent two angels in the forms of humans. They asked to enter upon him, but they found him on his day of worship, so the guards prevented them from entering, so they climbed over the sanctuary against him. They said: he did not perceive them while he was praying, until he saw them before him sitting. He said: he was frightened of them, and they said: ﴿Do not fear﴾, we are only ﴿two disputants, one of us has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth and do not be unjust﴾, meaning: do not fear. ﴿And guide us to the even path﴾: to the justice of judgment. He said: He said: "Relate to me your story." He said: one of them said: ﴿This brother of mine has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe﴾, so he wants to take my ewe, to complete his ewes to a hundred. He said: so he said to the other: "What do you say?" He said: "I have ninety-nine ewes, and this brother of mine has one ewe, so I want to take it from him, to complete my ewes to a hundred." He said: "And is he unwilling?" He said: "He is unwilling." He said: "And he is unwilling?" He said: "Then we will not leave you and that." He said: "You are not capable of that." He said: "If you go to pursue that or intend it, we will strike you here, here and here," and Asbat explained: the end of the nose, the root of the nose, and the forehead. He said: "O David, you are more deserving to be struck here, here and here, since you have ninety-nine wives, and Uriah had only one wife." Then she did not cease to put him in the way of death until he was killed, and his wife married. He said: then he looked and saw nothing, so he knew what he had fallen into and what he had been tested with. He said: so he fell down prostrating. He said: then he wept. He said: so he remained prostrating and weeping for forty days, not raising his head except for a need, then he would fall prostrate again weeping, then he would supplicate until grass grew from the tears of his eyes. He said: then God revealed to him after forty days: "O David, raise your head, for I have forgiven you." He said: "O Lord, how do I know that You have forgiven me, and You are a just judge who does not deviate in judgment? When Uriah comes on the Day of Resurrection, taking his head in his right hand or his left, his veins gushing with blood before Your Throne, he will say: 'O Lord, ask this one why he killed me?'" He said: then He revealed to him: "When that happens, I will call Uriah and ask him to grant you pardon, and he will grant it to me, and I will reward him with that with Paradise." He said: "O Lord, now I know that You have forgiven me." He said: so he could not bring himself to fill his eyes with the sky, out of shame before his Lord, until he died (ﷺ).

- Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, saying: Ata al-Khurasani narrated to me, saying: David engraved his sin on his palm so that he would not forget it. He said: whenever he saw it, his hand would tremble and shake.

Others said: rather, that was due to an impulse that arose in his soul, from thinking that he was able to complete a day in which he would not commit a sin, so he was tested with the trial with which he was tested on the day when he aspired within himself to complete it without committing a sin.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from al-Hasan: David divided time into four parts: a day for his wives, a day for his worship, a day for judging the Children of Israel, and a day for the Children of Israel, to remind them and be reminded by them, and to weep for them and have them weep for him. When it was the day of the Children of Israel, he said: they mentioned, and said: "Can a day come upon a man in which he does not commit a sin?" So David concealed in himself that he would be able to do that. When it was the day of his worship, he closed his doors and ordered that no one should enter upon him, and he devoted himself to the Torah. While he was reading it, suddenly a dove of gold with every beautiful color fell before him, and he reached out to take it. He said: it flew and landed not far away, without despairing him of itself. He said: he continued to follow it until he came upon a woman bathing, and her creation and beauty pleased him. He said: when she saw his shadow on the ground, she covered herself with her hair, and that increased his admiration for her. He had sent her husband with some of his armies, and he wrote to him to proceed to such and such a place, a place from which, if he went there, he would not return. He said: he did so, and he was killed. Then he proposed to her and married her. He said: Qatadah said: "We were informed that she was the mother of Solomon." He said: then while he was in the sanctuary, the two angels climbed over him. The disputants used to come to him from the gate of the sanctuary, so he was frightened of them when they climbed over the sanctuary. They said: ﴿Do not fear. Two disputants, one of us has wronged the other﴾ ... until ﴿and do not be unjust﴾, that is: do not incline. ﴿And guide us to the even path﴾, that is: to its justice and its goodness. ﴿This brother of mine has ninety-nine ewes﴾, and David had ninety-nine wives. ﴿And I have one ewe﴾, he said: the man had only one wife. ﴿So he says, "Entrust her to me, and he overpowers me in speech"﴾, that is: he wronged me and oppressed me. He said: ﴿He has certainly wronged you by asking for your ewe to be added to his ewes﴾ ... to His saying ﴿and few are they, and David thought﴾, so David knew that he was targeted by that, that is: it was meant by that. ﴿And fell down bowing and turned in repentance﴾. He said: in the report of Mutarrif, he prostrated for forty nights, until God revealed to him: "I have indeed forgiven you." He said: "O Lord, how can You forgive me while You are a just judge who wrongs no one?" He said: "I will judge in his favor, then I will ask him to grant you his blood or your sin, then I will reward him until he is pleased." He said: "Now my soul is at rest, and I know that You have forgiven me."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, saying: When the Children of Israel gathered around David, God sent down the Psalms (*al-Zabur*) to him, and taught him the craft of iron, and made it soft for him, and commanded the mountains and the birds to glorify God with him when he glorified Him. They claim that God did not give anyone of His creation a voice like his. When he recited the Psalms, they claim, the wild beasts would draw near to him until he took hold of their necks, and they would be listening, attentive to his voice. The devils made their musical instruments, lutes and cymbals, only according to the types of his voice. He was exceedingly diligent and constant in worship. He remained among the Children of Israel judging among them by the command of God as a prophet and successor. He was among the most diligent of the prophets and frequently wept. Then the trial of that woman befell him, which befell him. He had a sanctuary in which he would be alone for reciting the Psalms and for his prayer when he prayed. Below it was a garden belonging to a man of the Children of Israel, and the woman with whom David was afflicted was with that man...

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 24 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, that when Dawud (David) entered his prayer niche (mihrab) that day, he said: "No one shall enter upon me in my mihrab today until night, and nothing shall distract me from what I have set aside for myself until evening." He entered his mihrab and spread out his Psalms (Zabur) to read them. In the mihrab there was an opening (kuwwa) overlooking that garden. While he was sitting and reading the Zabur, a dove of gold came and landed in the opening. He raised his head and saw it, and it pleased him. Then he recalled what he had said: that nothing should distract him from what he had entered for. So he lowered his head and returned to his Zabur. The dove then flew toward the opening as a trial and a test, and landed before him. He took it in his hand, but it drew back not far off, so he followed it. It rose to the opening, and he took it in the opening. Then it flew toward the garden, and he followed it with his gaze to see where it would land. Behold, a woman was sitting bathing, in a form which only God knows in its beauty, loveliness and shape. They claim that when she saw him, she unbound her hair and covered her body with it, and he was captivated, and his heart was seized. He returned to his Zabur and his place, but she was in his thoughts and her remembrance never left his heart. The trial continued upon him until he sent her husband out to war. Then, as the People of the Book claim, he ordered the commander of his army to send her husband forward to places of death, until he was struck by some of what he intended for him of destruction. Dawud had ninety-nine wives. When her husband was killed, Dawud proposed to her and married her. Then God sent to him, while he was in his mihrab, two angels who came to him disputing, presenting a parable he struck for him and his companion. Dawud was startled only by them standing over his head in his mihrab. He said: "What brought you in upon me?" They said: "Do not fear. We have not entered for any harm or any suspicion. [Two adversaries, one of us has wronged the other,] so judge between us with truth, do not be unjust, and guide us to the right path." That is: carry us to the truth, and do not deviate with us from it. The angel who spoke said, concerning Uriah ibn Hananya, the husband of the woman: "This is my brother," that is, [of my religion]. "He has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe, and he says, 'Entrust it to me'," that is, carry me upon it. "And he overpowered me in speech," that is, he overcame me in argument, and he was stronger and more powerful than me, so he took my ewe to his ewes and left me with nothing. Dawud became angry and looked at the adversary who had not spoken, and said: "If he has spoken truthfully, I will strike between your eyes with an axe!" Then Dawud came to himself, and he understood that he himself was the one meant by what had been done concerning the wife of Uriah. He fell down prostrate, repentant, turning back, weeping, and he prostrated for forty mornings, fasting, neither eating nor drinking in them, until his tears made green plants grow beneath his face, and until the prostration wore away the flesh of his face. Then God accepted his repentance and received it from him.
It is claimed that he said: "My Lord, You have forgiven what I committed concerning the woman, so what of the blood of the wronged slain?" It was said to him: "O Dawud, as the People of the Book claim, indeed your Lord did not wrong him in his blood, but He will ask you about him and He will give him [recompense], and remove it from you." When what was upon Dawud was relieved, he marked his sin on the palm of his right hand, the inside of his palm. He never raised food or drink to his mouth without weeping when he saw it, and he never stood to address the people without spreading out his palm, so that the people faced it and could see the mark of his sin on his hand.

⁕ Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth mention, from Mujahid, who said: When Dawud committed the sin, he fell down prostrate before God for forty days, until from the tears of his eyes there grew plants of herbage that covered his head. Then he called out: "My Lord, my forehead has been wounded and my eye has become hard," and nothing of his sin had returned to him. So it was called out to him: "Is it a hungry one that you should be fed, or a sick one that you should be healed, or a wronged one that you should be given victory?" He said: then he wailed a wail that shook everything that had grown. At that point he was forgiven. His sin was written on his palm, which he would read. A vessel would be brought to him to drink, but he would drink only a third or half of it, and when he remembered his sin he would wail a wail such that his joints nearly separated from one another, and before he finished his drink he would fill it with his tears. It was said: the tear of Dawud equals the tears of all creation, and the tear of Adam equals the tear of Dawud and the tears of all creation. He said: On the Day of Resurrection he will come with his sin written on his palm, and he will say: "My Lord, my sin, my sin, bring me forward." He said: he will be brought forward, but he will not feel safe, and he will say: "My Lord, delay me," and he will be delayed, but he will not feel safe.

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a informed me, from Abu Sakhr, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, that he heard him say: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Dawud the Prophet (ﷺ), when he looked at the woman and was seized with desire, cut off [the troops] to the Children of Israel, and he instructed the commander of the expedition, saying: When the enemy is present, bring forward so-and-so before the Ark (al-tabut), and in that time the Ark was sought for victory. Whoever was sent forward before the Ark did not return until he was slain or the army was routed from him. So the woman's husband was killed, and the two angels descended upon Dawud, relating to him his story. Dawud became aware and prostrated. He remained prostrate for forty nights, until the crops grew from his tears upon his head, and the earth ate his forehead while he was saying in his prostration..." Of al-Raqashi I did not retain anything except these words: "My Lord, Dawud has slipped, further than the distance between east and west. If You do not have mercy on the weakness of Dawud and forgive his sin, I will make his sin a tale among the successors after him." Then Jibril (ﷺ) came to him after the forty nights and said: "O Dawud, God has indeed forgiven you the desire you had." Dawud said: "I know that the Lord is able to forgive me the desire I had, and I know that God is just and does not incline. So what of such-and-such when he comes on the Day of Resurrection and says: 'O Lord, my blood which is with Dawud'?" Jibril (ﷺ) said: "I did not ask your Lord about that, but if you wish, I will do it." He said: "Yes." So Jibril ascended, and Dawud prostrated. He remained as long as God willed, then descended and said: "O Dawud, I have asked your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, about that for which you sent me, and He said: Say to Dawud: God will gather you both on the Day of Resurrection, and He will say: 'Give me your blood which is with Dawud,' and he will say: 'It is yours, O Lord.' He will say: 'Then for you in Paradise is whatever you wish and desire, as recompense.'"

⁕ Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jabir narrated to us, from Ata al-Khurasani: that the letter of the commander of the expedition came announcing the death of those who had been slain. When Dawud read the announcement of a man among them, he turned back, and when he reached the man's name he said: "God has decreed death upon every soul." He said: When her waiting period had ended, he proposed to her.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verses 25–26:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So We forgave him that; and indeed, for him with Us is a near approach and a good return (25). O David, indeed We have made you a successor (khalifa) upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow [your own] desire, for it will lead you astray from the way of Allah. Indeed, those who go astray from the way of Allah will have a severe punishment for having forgotten the Day of Account (26).﴾

His, the Exalted's, words ﴿So We forgave him that﴾ mean: So We pardoned him and overlooked for him, not holding him to account for that sin and offense. ﴿And indeed, for him with Us is a near approach﴾ means: indeed, for him with Us is nearness to Us on the Day of Resurrection.

Concerning His words ﴿So We forgave him that﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said what we have said.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿So We forgave him that﴾: the sin.

* *

As for His words ﴿and a good return﴾:

He says: a place of return and a destination to which he returns on the Day of Resurrection.

The people of interpretation said what we have said concerning this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and a good return﴾: meaning a good destination.

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿and a good return﴾, he said: a good place of return.

* *

As for His words ﴿O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth﴾:

His, the Exalted's, words mean: And We said to David: O David, indeed We have appointed you as a successor upon the earth after those of Our messengers who were before you, as a judge among its people.

As follows:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿indeed We have made you a successor﴾: He made him a king over the earth. ﴿So judge between the people in truth﴾: meaning, with justice and equity. ﴿And do not follow desire﴾: meaning, do not prefer your desire in your judgment between them over truth and justice in it, lest you deviate from the truth. ﴿For it will lead you astray from the way of Allah﴾: meaning, your following of your desire in your judgment will incline you away from justice and acting by the truth, away from the way of Allah which He has set for the people of faith, and then you will be among the ruined because of your going astray from the way of Allah.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, those who go astray from the way of Allah will have a severe punishment for having forgotten the Day of Account﴾:

His, the Exalted's, words mean: Indeed, those who incline away from the way of Allah, which is the truth He prescribed for His servants and commanded them to act upon, and who deviate from it in this world, will have, in the Hereafter, on the Day of Account, a severe punishment for their going astray from the way of Allah, for having forgotten the command of Allah. That is: for having abandoned judging with justice and acting in obedience to Allah. ﴿on the Day of Account﴾ is connected to the severe punishment.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said regarding the interpretation of this.

Those who said that:

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: al-Awwam informed us, from Ikrima, regarding His words ﴿a severe punishment for having forgotten the Day of Account﴾, he said: this is from the inversion of word order (al-taqdim wa'l-ta'khir), meaning: for them on the Day of Account is a severe punishment for having forgotten.

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿for having forgotten the Day of Account﴾, he said: nusu (they forgot): they abandoned.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verses 27–29:

Concerning the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve, from the Fire.﴾ (27) ﴿Or shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters in the earth? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked?﴾ (28) ﴿[This is] a Book which We have sent down to you, blessed, that they may ponder its verses and that those of understanding may be reminded.﴾ (29)

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them﴾ in vain or in play. We did not create them except that obedience to Us be carried out within them, and that it end in Our command and Our prohibition.

﴿That is the assumption of those who disbelieve﴾ means: that is the assumption that We created that as falsehood and play, the assumption of those who disbelieve in God, so they do not affirm His oneness, and do not know His greatness, and that He should not act in vain, so that they would be certain thereby that He does not create anything in vain. ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾ means: from the Fire of Hell.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Or shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters in the earth﴾

He says: Shall We treat those who affirmed God and His Messenger and acted by what God commanded, and refrained from what He forbade them, ﴿like the corrupters in the earth﴾? He says: like those who associate partners with God, disobey Him, and oppose His command and prohibition.

﴿Or shall We treat the righteous﴾ means: those who feared God through obedience to Him and watched over Him, so they guarded against His disobedience ﴿like the wicked﴾ means: like the disbelievers who violate the sacred things of God.

* *

And His saying: ﴿[This is] a Book which We have sent down to you﴾

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: this Qur'an is ﴿a Book which We have sent down to you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿blessed, that they may ponder its verses﴾ means: that they may ponder the proofs of God that are in it, and what laws He has prescribed in it, so that they may be admonished and act upon it.

The reciters differed regarding the reading of this. The majority of reciters read ﴿liyaddabbaru﴾ (that they may ponder) with the yāʾ, meaning: that those to whom We have sent you, O Muhammad, from your people, may ponder this Qur'an. And Abu Jaʿfar and ʿAsim read "litaddabbaru āyātihi" with the tāʾ, meaning: that you yourself, O Muhammad, and your followers may ponder it.

The more correct of the two readings in our view is to say: they are two well-known readings, both sound in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct. ﴿And that those of understanding may be reminded﴾ means: and that people of intellect and discernment may take heed of the signs in this Book, so that they may turn back from the error they persist in, and proceed to the right guidance and path of correctness that it has indicated to them.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) have said something similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿those of understanding﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿those of understanding﴾: "those of intellect among people." We have already explained this previously with its evidences, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 38, verses 30–33:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave to David, Solomon. How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who turned back [to Allah] often. When there were displayed before him, at the hour of sunset, the poised [steeds], swift of pace.﴾ [...] ﴿So he said, "Indeed, I have loved the good [of horses] in preference to the remembrance of my Lord" until they [i.e., the steeds] disappeared behind the veil. "Return them to me." So he began to pass his hand over [their] legs and necks.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And We gave to David, Solomon﴾ — meaning, a son for him — ﴿How excellent a servant!﴾ — meaning: how excellent a servant Solomon was — ﴿Indeed, he was one who turned back [to Allah] often﴾ — meaning: indeed, he returned to the obedience of Allah, turning to Him repentantly from what displeased Him. It was also said that what is meant is that he remembered Allah and obeyed Him much.

Those who said this:

– Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who turned back often﴾: He said, "The awwab is the one who glorifies [Allah]."

– Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who turned back often﴾: He said, "He was obedient to Allah, and much given to prayer."

– Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, [concerning] his saying ﴿How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who turned back often﴾: He said, "The one who glorifies [Allah]."

The one who glorifies [Allah] may be [so] in prayer and in remembrance. We have already explained the meaning of awwab, and mentioned the differences of the exegetes concerning it earlier, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary.

* *

And His saying ﴿When there were displayed before him, at the hour of sunset, the poised [steeds], swift of pace﴾

* *

He says: "Indeed, I loved the good until I became heedless of the remembrance of my Lord and of performing His obligation." It was also said that this was the 'Asr prayer.

The exegetes have said things similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

– Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿in preference to the remembrance of my Lord﴾ — from the 'Asr prayer.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam told us, saying: Abu Zur'ah told us, saying: Haywah ibn Shurayh told us, saying: Abu Sakhr told us, that he heard Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from the people of Kufa, say: I heard Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri say: I asked 'Ali ibn Abi Talib about the middle prayer, and he said: "It is the 'Asr, and it is the one with which Solomon ibn Dawud was tested."

* *

And His saying ﴿until they disappeared behind the veil﴾

He says: "until the sun disappeared behind the veil," meaning: it set in its setting.

As:

* *

Those who said this:

– Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "So he began to pass his hand over [their] legs and necks" — he struck their shanks and necks.

– Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bazi' told us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: "He ordered them and they were hamstrung."

Those who said this:

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 38, verses 30–33:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave to David, Solomon. How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who turned back [to Allah] often. When there were displayed before him, at the hour of sunset, the poised [steeds], swift of pace.﴾ [...] ﴿So he said, "Indeed, I have loved the good [of horses] in preference to the remembrance of my Lord" until they [i.e., the steeds] disappeared behind the veil. "Return them to me." So he began to pass his hand over [their] legs and necks.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And We gave to David, Solomon﴾ — meaning, a son for him — ﴿How excellent a servant!﴾ — meaning: how excellent a servant Solomon was — ﴿Indeed, he was one who turned back [to Allah] often﴾ — meaning: indeed, he returned to the obedience of Allah, turning to Him repentantly from what displeased Him. It was also said that what is meant is that he remembered Allah and obeyed Him much.

Those who said this:

– Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who turned back often﴾: He said, "The awwab is the one who glorifies [Allah]."
