– Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "until they disappeared behind the veil" — until it set.

* *

And His saying ﴿Return them to me﴾

He says: "Return to me the horses which were displayed before me, which occupied me from the prayer," so they returned them to him.

As:

– Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "Return them to me" — he said, "The horses."

* *

And His saying ﴿So he began to pass his hand over [their] legs and necks﴾

He says: he began to pass his hand over their shanks (al-suq, the plural of al-saq) and necks.

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of Solomon's "passing over" the shanks and necks of these swift horses. Some of them said: the meaning is that he hamstrung them and struck off their necks, from the expression "masaha 'ulawatahu," meaning he struck his neck.

Those who said this:

– Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: "So he began to pass his hand over [their] legs and necks" — he said: Al-Hasan said: "He said, 'No, by Allah, they shall not distract me from the worship of my Lord; the last of what is upon you...'" — he said his statement concerning it, meaning Qatadah and al-Hasan. He said: "So he slashed their hamstrings and struck off their necks."

– Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "So he began to pass his hand over [their] legs and necks" — he struck their shanks and necks.

– Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bazi' told us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: "He ordered them and they were hamstrung."

Others said: rather, he began to pass his hand over their manes and hamstrings out of love for them.

Those who said this:

– 'Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿So he began to pass his hand over [their] legs and necks﴾: He says, "He began to pass his hand over the manes of the horses and their hamstrings, out of love for them."

And this view which we have mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas is more fitting to the interpretation of the verse, because the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) would not, Allah willing, punish an animal by hamstringing it, and destroy a part of his property without cause, merely because he was occupied from his prayer by looking at them; and the horses bear no fault for his being occupied by looking at them.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 38, verses 30–33:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave to David, Solomon. How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who turned back [to Allah] often. When there were displayed before him, at the hour of sunset, the poised [steeds], swift of pace.﴾ [...] ﴿So he said, "Indeed, I have loved the good [of horses] in preference to the remembrance of my Lord" until they [i.e., the steeds] disappeared behind the veil. "Return them to me." So he began to pass his hand over [their] legs and necks.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And We gave to David, Solomon﴾ — meaning, a son for him — ﴿How excellent a servant!﴾ — meaning: how excellent a servant Solomon was — ﴿Indeed, he was one who turned back [to Allah] often﴾ — meaning: indeed, he returned to the obedience of Allah, turning to Him repentantly from what displeased Him. It was also said that what is meant is that he remembered Allah and obeyed Him much.

Those who said this:

– Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who turned back often﴾: He said, "The awwab is the one who glorifies [Allah]."

– Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who turned back often﴾: He said, "He was obedient to Allah, and much given to prayer."

– Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, [concerning] his saying ﴿How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who turned back often﴾: He said, "The one who glorifies [Allah]."

The one who glorifies [Allah] may be [so] in prayer and in remembrance. We have already explained the meaning of awwab, and mentioned the differences of the exegetes concerning it earlier, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary.

* *

And His saying ﴿When there were displayed before him, at the hour of sunset, the poised [steeds], swift of pace﴾

His saying, may He be exalted, meaning: indeed, he turned back to Allah from his sin which he committed, when there were displayed before him at sunset the poised [steeds]. So "when" (idh) is connected to "awwab". "Al-safinat" is the plural of "al-safin" among horses, and its feminine is "safinah". Among some Arabs, "al-safin" is the one that gathers together its two forelegs and bends the tip of the hoof of one of its hind legs; and among others, it is the one that gathers its forelegs together. Al-Farra' asserted that "al-safin" is the one standing, from which it is said: "safanat al-khayl yasfinu sufunan" (the horses stood).

The exegetes have said things similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

– Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah ﴿the poised [steeds], swift of pace﴾: He said, "The sufun of the horse is raising one of its forelegs until it is on the tip of the hoof."

– Al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Safana al-faras: he raised one of his forelegs until it was on the tip of the hoof."

– Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿When there were displayed before him, at the hour of sunset, the poised [steeds], swift of pace﴾ — he said, "meaning: the horses, and their sufun is their standing and spreading their legs."

– Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "al-safinat" — he said, "the horses."

– Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿al-safinat al-jiyad﴾: He said, "The horses which Satan brought out for Solomon from one of the meadows of the sea." He said: "The horses, mules and donkeys stand (tasfinu) on three, raising one leg until the tip of the hoof is on the ground. [Note: We did not find "al-safn" with a sukun on the fa' as a verbal noun of "safanat al-khayl"; its verbal noun is "al-sufun", like "jalasa yajlisu juluusan", which is the analogical form, because the verb is intransitive; and "al-safn" is the verbal noun for the transitive form.]"

– Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "al-safinat: the horses, and they had wings."

As for al-jiyad, they are the swift ones; its singular is jawad.

As:

– Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "al-jiyad: the swift ones."

It is mentioned that they were twenty mares with wings.

Report concerning that:

– Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Mu'ammal told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from his father, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, concerning His saying ﴿When there were displayed before him, at the hour of sunset, the poised [steeds], swift of pace﴾: He said, "They were twenty horses with wings."

* *

And His saying ﴿So he said, "Indeed, I have loved the good [of horses] in preference to the remembrance of my Lord" until they disappeared behind the veil﴾

In this statement there is an omitted part, which is dispensed with by the apparent meaning: "so he was heedless of the prayer until it passed him, and he said: 'Indeed, I have loved the good.'" And by His saying "So he said, 'Indeed, I have loved the good'" he means: the wealth and the horses, or the good of wealth.

– Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi: ﴿So he said, "Indeed, I have loved the good"﴾: He said, "The horses."

– Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, [concerning] his saying ﴿Indeed, I have loved the good﴾: He said, "The wealth."

* *

And His saying ﴿in preference to the remembrance of my Lord﴾

He says: "Indeed, I loved the good until I became heedless of the remembrance of my Lord and of performing His obligation." It was also said that this was the 'Asr prayer.

The exegetes have said things similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

– Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: ﴿in preference to the remembrance of my Lord﴾ — from the 'Asr prayer.

– Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿in preference to the remembrance of my Lord﴾ — he said: "The 'Asr prayer." Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam told us, saying: Abu Zur'ah told us, saying: Haywah ibn Shurayh told us, saying: Abu Sakhr told us, that he heard Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from the people of Kufa, say: I heard Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri say: I asked 'Ali ibn Abi Talib about the middle prayer, and he said: "It is the 'Asr, and it is the one with which Solomon ibn Dawud was tested."

* *

And His saying ﴿until they disappeared behind the veil﴾

He says: "until the sun disappeared behind the veil," meaning: it set in its setting.

As:

– Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salamah told us, saying: Mika'il told us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, I have loved the good in preference to the remembrance of my Lord until they disappeared behind the veil﴾: He said, "The sun disappeared from behind an emerald green [veil], so the greenness of the sky came from it."

– Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: "until they disappeared behind the veil" — until it sank below the horizon. Qatadah said: "By Allah, the Children of Israel did not dispute with him, nor did they oppose him, but they left him with what Allah had left him."

– Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "until they disappeared behind the veil" — until it set.

* *

And His saying ﴿Return them to me﴾

He says: "Return to me the horses which were displayed before me, which occupied me from the prayer," so they returned them to him.

As:

– Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "Return them to me" — he said, "The horses."

* *

And His saying ﴿So he began to pass his hand over [their] legs and necks﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 34–35:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did try Solomon and We placed upon his throne a body; then he turned back in repentance. He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me; indeed, You are the Bestower."﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And We did test Solomon, and We placed upon his throne a body," a devil in the form of a man. They mention that his name was Sakhr. It was also said that his name was Asaf. It was also said that his name was Asir. It was also said that his name was Habqiq.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and We placed upon his throne a body﴾, he said: It was Sakhr the jinn, who took the form of a body upon his throne.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying (And We did try Solomon and We placed upon his throne a body; then he turned back in repentance). He said: The body was the devil to whom Solomon had handed his ring, and he threw it into the sea; Solomon's kingdom was in his ring. The name of the jinn was Sakhr.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Hasan, ﴿and We placed upon his throne a body﴾, he said: a devil.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and We placed upon his throne a body﴾, he said: a devil called Asir.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿upon his throne a body﴾, he said: a devil called Asaf. Solomon said to him: "How do you test people?" He said: "Show me your ring and I will tell you." When he gave it to him, Asaf threw it into the sea, and Solomon wandered off, and his kingdom was lost. Asaf sat on his throne, and God prevented Solomon's wives from him, so he did not approach them, and they rejected him. He said: So Solomon would beg for food, saying: "Do you know me? Feed me, I am Solomon," and they would deny him, until a woman gave him a fish one day, which she had cleaned, and he found his ring in its belly. His kingdom returned to him, and Asaf fled and entered the sea running away.

al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that in his narration he said: he would say: "If only you knew me, you would have fed me."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And We did try Solomon and We placed upon his throne a body; then he turned back in repentance﴾, he said: Qatadah told us that Solomon ordered the building of Bayt al-Maqdis, and it was said to him: "Build it without any sound of iron being heard in it." He sought that but could not achieve it, and it was said to him: "There is a devil in the sea called Sakhr, resembling a giant." So he sought him. There was a spring in the sea that he would visit once every seven days; its water was drained and wine was put into it. When the day of his visit came, he found wine and said: "You are indeed a good drink, but you afflict the forbearing and increase the ignorant in ignorance." Then he returned, and grew very thirsty, then came to it again and said: "You are indeed a good drink, but you afflict the forbearing and increase the ignorant in ignorance." Then he drank it until it overcame his mind. He was shown the ring, or it was sealed with it between his shoulders, and he was humbled. His kingdom was in his ring. He brought him to Solomon, who said: "We have been ordered to build this house, and we were told: let no sound of iron be heard in it." So the hoopoe's eggs were brought, and a glass was placed over them. The hoopoe came and circled around it, seeing its eggs but unable to reach them. It went and brought a diamond and placed it upon it, and cut through it until it reached its eggs. They took the diamond and began cutting stones with it. Solomon, whenever he wished to enter the latrine or the bath, would not enter with his ring. One day he went to the bath, and that devil Sakhr was with him, and that was at the time of a sin committed with some of his wives. He entered the bath and gave the devil his ring, and he threw it into the sea, and a fish swallowed it, and Solomon's kingdom was taken from him, and the likeness of Solomon was cast upon the devil. He came and sat on his throne and bed, and he was given authority over all of Solomon's kingdom except his wives. He began judging among them, and they began to disapprove of many things from him, until they said: "The prophet of God has been tested." There was a man among them whom they compared to Umar ibn al-Khattab in strength, and he said: "By God, I will test him." He said to him: "O Prophet of God," while he appeared to be only the prophet of God: "One of us is struck by janabah on a cold night, and he deliberately leaves washing until the sun rises; do you see any harm in him?" He said: "No." He said: So while he was like that for forty nights, until the prophet of God found his ring in the belly of a fish. He came, and no jinn or bird met him without prostrating to him, until he reached them. ﴿and We placed upon his throne a body﴾, he said: It was the devil Sakhr.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿And We did try Solomon﴾, he said: We tested him. ﴿and We placed upon his throne a body﴾, he said: the devil, when he sat on his throne for forty days. He said: Solomon had a hundred wives, and one of them was called Jaradah, who was the dearest of his wives to him and the most trusted by him, and when he was in a state of janabah or went to relieve himself, he would take off his ring, and no one among the people was trusted with it except her. One day she came to him and said: "My brother and so-and-so have a dispute, and I would love for you to judge in his favour when he comes to you." He said to her: "Yes," but did not do so. So he was tested and gave her his ring, and entered the privy. The devil came out in his form and said to her: "Give me the ring," and she gave it to him. He came and sat in Solomon's seat. Solomon came out afterwards and asked her to give him his ring, and she said: "Did you not take it before?" He said: "No," and he went out wandering in his place. He said: The devil remained judging among the people for forty days. He said: The people rejected his rulings, so the readers of the Children of Israel and their scholars gathered, and they came and entered upon his wives, and said: "We have rejected this; if this is Solomon, then his mind has gone, and we have rejected his rulings." He said: The women wept at that. He said: Then they came walking until they reached him, surrounded him, then unfolded the Torah and read. He said: Then he flew from among them until he landed on a balcony with the ring with him, then he flew until he went to the sea, and the ring fell from him into the sea, and a fish of the sea's fish swallowed it. He said: Solomon came in his state until he reached a fisherman of the sea's fishermen, and he was hungry, his hunger intensified, so he asked them for some of their catch. He said: "I am Solomon," so one of them stood up and struck him with a stick and split his head, and he began washing his blood while on the seashore. The fishermen blamed their companion who had struck him and said: "What a bad thing you did in striking him." He said: "He claimed to be Solomon." He said: They gave him two fish from what had spoiled among them, and the harm he had suffered did not distract him, until he went to the shore of the sea, split their bellies, and began washing... and found his ring in the belly of one of them. He took it and put it on, and God restored to him his splendour and his kingdom. The birds came and hovered over him, and the people knew that he was Solomon, and they stood apologising for what they had done. He said: "I do not praise you for your excuse, nor do I blame you for what happened from you; this matter had to happen." He said: So he came until he reached his kingdom, and he sent for the devil and he was brought. On that day God subjected the wind and the devils to him, which had not been subjected to him before. This is His saying: ﴿grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me; indeed, You are the Bestower﴾. He said: He sent for the devil and he was brought, and he ordered him to be placed in an iron chest, then it was closed and locked with a lock, and sealed with his ring. Then he ordered it to be thrown into the sea, where it remains until the Hour arrives. His name was Habqiq.

* *

His saying ﴿then he turned back in repentance﴾

Solomon returned to his kingdom after his kingdom had departed from him and gone.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

It was reported to me from al-Muharibi, from Abd al-Rahman, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿then he turned back in repentance﴾, he said: Solomon entered upon a woman who sold fish, bought a fish from her, split its belly, and found his ring. He did not pass by any tree, stone, or anything without prostrating to him, until he reached his kingdom and his family. That is His saying: ﴿then he turned back in repentance﴾, meaning: then he returned.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿then he turned back in repentance﴾, meaning Solomon came back and returned.

* *

His saying ﴿He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me"﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Solomon said, turning eagerly to his Lord: "My Lord, conceal my sin which I committed between me and You, so that You do not punish me for it," ﴿and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me﴾, which none of you may strip from me as it was stripped from me before by this devil.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me"﴾, he says: a kingdom that I will not be stripped of as I was stripped. Some of the grammarians of Arabic interpreted the meaning of His saying ﴿such as will not belong to anyone after me﴾ as: that it should not belong to anyone after me, as Ibn Ahmar said:

What is the mother of Ghafr upon the black-mottled Da'jaa, whom the ram-like mountain goats with their wild, sure-footed climbing drive away from her?

On the top of a smooth, bald height, lofty in the sky, no plain nor mountain is fitting beyond it.

The meaning: there is no plain or mountain above it that is more fortified than it.

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾

He says: Indeed You are the Bestower of whatever You will upon whomever You will; in Your hand are the treasuries of everything; You open from that whatever You wish for whomever You wish.

His kingdom returned to him, and Asaf fled and entered the sea running away.

al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that in his narration he said: he would say: "If only you knew me, you would have fed me."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And We did try Solomon and We placed upon his throne a body; then he turned back in repentance﴾, he said: Qatadah told us that Solomon ordered the building of Bayt al-Maqdis, and it was said to him: "Build it without any sound of iron being heard in it." He sought that but could not achieve it, and it was said to him: "There is a devil in the sea called Sakhr, resembling a giant." So he sought him. There was a spring in the sea that he would visit once every seven days; its water was drained and wine was put into it. When the day of his visit came, he found wine and said: "You are indeed a good drink, but you afflict the forbearing and increase the ignorant in ignorance." Then he returned, and grew very thirsty, then came to it again and said: "You are indeed a good drink, but you afflict the forbearing and increase the ignorant in ignorance." Then he drank it until it overcame his mind. He was shown the ring, or it was sealed with it between his shoulders, and he was humbled. His kingdom was in his ring. He brought him to Solomon, who said: "We have been ordered to build this house, and we were told: let no sound of iron be heard in it." So the hoopoe's eggs were brought, and a glass was placed over them. The hoopoe came and circled around it, seeing its eggs but unable to reach them. It went and brought a diamond and placed it upon it, and cut through it until it reached its eggs. They took the diamond and began cutting stones with it. Solomon, whenever he wished to enter the latrine or the bath, would not enter with his ring. One day he went to the bath, and that devil Sakhr was with him, and that was at the time of a sin committed with some of his wives. He entered the bath and gave the devil his ring, and he threw it into the sea, and a fish swallowed it, and Solomon's kingdom was taken from him, and the likeness of Solomon was cast upon the devil. He came and sat on his throne and bed, and he was given authority over all of Solomon's kingdom except his wives. He began judging among them, and they began to disapprove of many things from him, until they said: "The prophet of God has been tested." There was a man among them whom they compared to Umar ibn al-Khattab in strength, and he said: "By God, I will test him." He said to him: "O Prophet of God," while he appeared to be only the prophet of God: "One of us is struck by janabah on a cold night, and he deliberately leaves washing until the sun rises; do you see any harm in him?" He said: "No." He said: So while he was like that for forty nights, until the prophet of God found his ring in the belly of a fish. He came, and no jinn or bird met him without prostrating to him, until he reached them. ﴿and We placed upon his throne a body﴾, he said: It was the devil Sakhr.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿And We did try Solomon﴾, he said: We tested him. ﴿and We placed upon his throne a body﴾, he said: the devil, when he sat on his throne for forty days. He said: Solomon had a hundred wives, and one of them was called Jaradah, who was the dearest of his wives to him and the most trusted by him, and when he was in a state of janabah or went to relieve himself, he would take off his ring, and no one among the people was trusted with it except her. One day she came to him and said: "My brother and so-and-so have a dispute, and I would love for you to judge in his favour when he comes to you." He said to her: "Yes," but did not do so. So he was tested and gave her his ring, and entered the privy. The devil came out in his form and said to her: "Give me the ring," and she gave it to him. He came and sat in Solomon's seat. Solomon came out afterwards and asked her to give him his ring, and she said: "Did you not take it before?" He said: "No," and he went out wandering in his place. He said: The devil remained judging among the people for forty days. He said: The people rejected his rulings, so the readers of the Children of Israel and their scholars gathered, and they came and entered upon his wives, and said: "We have rejected this; if this is Solomon, then his mind has gone, and we have rejected his rulings." He said: The women wept at that. He said: Then they came walking until they reached him, surrounded him, then unfolded the Torah and read. He said: Then he flew from among them until he landed on a balcony with the ring with him, then he flew until he went to the sea, and the ring fell from him into the sea, and a fish of the sea's fish swallowed it. He said: Solomon came in his state until he reached a fisherman of the sea's fishermen, and he was hungry, his hunger intensified, so he asked them for some of their catch. He said: "I am Solomon," so one of them stood up and struck him with a stick and split his head, and he began washing his blood while on the seashore. The fishermen blamed their companion who had struck him and said: "What a bad thing you did in striking him." He said: "He claimed to be Solomon." He said: They gave him two fish from what had spoiled among them, and the harm he had suffered did not distract him, until he went to the shore of the sea, split their bellies, and began washing... and found his ring in the belly of one of them. He took it and put it on, and God restored to him his splendour and his kingdom. The birds came and hovered over him, and the people knew that he was Solomon, and they stood apologising for what they had done. He said: "I do not praise you for your excuse, nor do I blame you for what happened from you; this matter had to happen." He said: So he came until he reached his kingdom, and he sent for the devil and he was brought. On that day God subjected the wind and the devils to him, which had not been subjected to him before. This is His saying: ﴿grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me; indeed, You are the Bestower﴾. He said: He sent for the devil and he was brought, and he ordered him to be placed in an iron chest, then it was closed and locked with a lock, and sealed with his ring. Then he ordered it to be thrown into the sea, where it remains until the Hour arrives. His name was Habqiq.

* *

His saying ﴿then he turned back in repentance﴾

Solomon returned to his kingdom after his kingdom had departed from him and gone.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

It was reported to me from al-Muharibi, from Abd al-Rahman, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿then he turned back in repentance﴾, he said: Solomon entered upon a woman who sold fish, bought a fish from her, split its belly, and found his ring. He did not pass by any tree, stone, or anything without prostrating to him, until he reached his kingdom and his family. That is His saying: ﴿then he turned back in repentance﴾, meaning: then he returned.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿then he turned back in repentance﴾, meaning Solomon came back and returned.

* *

His saying ﴿He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me"﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Solomon said, turning eagerly to his Lord: "My Lord, conceal my sin which I committed between me and You, so that You do not punish me for it," ﴿and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me﴾, which none of you may strip from me as it was stripped from me before by this devil.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me"﴾, he says: a kingdom that I will not be stripped of as I was stripped. Some of the grammarians of Arabic interpreted the meaning of His saying ﴿such as will not belong to anyone after me﴾ as: that it should not belong to anyone after me, as Ibn Ahmar said:

What is the mother of Ghafr upon the black-mottled Da'jaa, whom the ram-like mountain goats with their wild, sure-footed climbing drive away from her?

On the top of a smooth, bald height, lofty in the sky, no plain nor mountain is fitting beyond it.

The meaning: there is no plain or mountain above it that is more fortified than it.

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾

He says: Indeed You are the Bestower of whatever You will upon whomever You will; in Your hand are the treasuries of everything; You open from that whatever You wish for whomever You wish.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 36–40:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he directed﴾ [36], ﴿and the devils, every builder and diver﴾ [37], ﴿and others bound together in shackles﴾ [38], ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾ [39], ﴿and indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾ [40].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So We answered his supplication and gave him a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him. ﴿So We subjected to him the wind﴾ in place of the horses which had distracted him from prayer, ﴿running gently by his command﴾, meaning: soft and gentle, and it is from rukhawa (softness).

As follows:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Buzayʿ narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, that the Prophet of Allah Sulayman (ﷺ), when the horses were presented to him, the looking at them distracted him from the afternoon prayer ﴿until they were hidden by the veil﴾, so he became angry for the sake of Allah, and ordered them to be hamstrung, and Allah replaced them with something swifter than them: He subjected the wind, running gently by his command wherever he wished. So he would set out in the morning from Iliya, take his midday rest at Qazwin, then set out from Qazwin and spend the night at Kabul.

• I was told, from al-Ḥasan, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying ﴿And grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me﴾: he supplicated on a day when he supplicated, and he did not have the wind in his kingdom, nor every builder and diver among the devils. So he called upon his Lord at his repentance and seeking forgiveness, and Allah granted him what he asked, and his kingdom was completed.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of rukhaʾ (gentle). Some of them said regarding it something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿running gently by his command﴾ he said: good (ṭayyiba).

• al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he directed﴾, he said: swift and good; he said: not violent nor slow.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿gently﴾: rukhaʾ is the gentle one.

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAmir narrated to us, saying: Qurra narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His saying ﴿gently wherever he directed﴾, he said: not violent, nor is the moderate in between called rukhaʾ.

Others said: the meaning is: obedient to Sulayman.

Those who said that:

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying ﴿gently﴾: it means obedient to him.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿running gently by his command﴾, he said: by rukhaʾ is meant: obedient.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Nuʿman al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abu Rajaʾ, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His saying ﴿running gently by his command﴾, he said: obedient.

• I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying ﴿gently﴾: it means obedient.

• Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿gently﴾, he said: willingly.

* *

As for His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾:

It means: wherever he willed, from their saying: "Allah granted you good" (aṣāba Allāhu bika khayran), i.e., Allah willed good for you.

Interpreters said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾: it means wherever he willed.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾: wherever he willed, he settled upon it.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Nuʿman al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abu Rajaʾ, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: to wherever he willed.

• I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih ﴿wherever he directed﴾: that is, wherever he willed.

• Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We subjected the devils to him, giving him power over them in place of what We tested him with, when We cast upon his throne one of them. He used them for whatever works he willed, among them builders and divers. The builders among them made sanctuaries (maḥārīb) and statues, the divers extracted ornaments for him from the seas, and others carved for him basins and cooking pots, while the rebellious ones were bound in chains.

As follows:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾, he said: they worked for him whatever he willed of sanctuaries and statues, and divers who extracted ornaments from the sea. ﴿And others bound together in shackles﴾, he said: the rebellious devils in chains.

• I was told, from al-Maḥāribī, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾, he said: this was not in the kingdom of Dawud; Allah gave him the kingdom of Dawud and added to it the wind. ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver, and others bound together in shackles﴾, he said: meaning in chains.

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿al-asfad﴾, he said: it gathers the two hands to the neck; and al-asfad is the plural of ṣafad, which are shackles.

* *

As for His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾:

The interpreters differed concerning what is indicated by His saying ﴿this﴾ of the gift, and which gift is meant by His saying "Our gift". Some of them said: it refers to the kingdom which Allah gave him.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: al-Ḥasan said: the kingdom which We gave you; give what you wish and withhold what you wish.

• al-Maḥāribī narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak ﴿This is Our gift﴾: this is Our kingdom.

Others said: rather, it means His subjecting the devils to him, and they said: the meaning of the speech is: this which We have given you, from every builder and diver among the devils and others, is Our gift.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: these devils, imprison whomever you wish of them in your bonds and your punishment, or release whomever you wish of them, earning thereby a favour; do what you wish.

Others said: rather, it is the strength for intercourse which he had been given.

Those who said that:

• I was told, from Abu Yusuf, from Saʿid ibn Ṭarif, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Sulayman had in his loins the semen of a hundred men, and he had three hundred wives and nine hundred concubines: ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾.

The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying which we have mentioned from al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥak, that by the gift is meant the kingdom which He, may His remembrance be exalted, gave him. This is because He, may His majesty be praised, mentioned it following His report of the request of His Prophet Sulayman, peace and blessings be upon him, for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him; He informed that He subjected to him what was not subjected to any of the children of Adam, namely the wind and the devils as described. Then He, may His majesty be glorified, said to him: This which We have given you of the kingdom, and Our subjecting to you what We have subjected, is Our gift, and We have granted you what you asked Us to grant you of the kingdom that would not befit anyone after you ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾.

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of His saying ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾. Some of them said: it means: give to whomever you wish of the kingdom We have given you, and withhold from whomever you wish, there is no account upon you in that.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Ḥasan said: ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾: the kingdom which We gave you; give what you wish and withhold what you wish, there is no consequence or account upon you.

• I was told, from al-Maḥāribī, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾: he asked for a kingdom that is pleasant, not to be called to account for on the Day of Resurrection; so He said: whatever you give and whatever you withhold, there is no blame upon you.

• Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from ʿIkrima ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: give or withhold, there is no account upon you.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿so grant﴾, he said: give or withhold without account.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: free from these devils whom We subjected to you for service, or from the bonds, of those who were among them bound in shackles, whomever you wish, and imprison whomever you wish; there is no blame upon you in that.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: these devils, imprison whomever you wish of them in your bonds and your punishment, and release whomever you wish of them, earning thereby a favour; do what you wish, there is no account upon you in that.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: free from the jinn whomever you wish, and withhold whomever you wish. Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: you bestow upon whomever you wish of them, freeing him, and withhold whomever you wish, employing him; there is no account upon you in that.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: this which We have given you of the strength for intercourse is Our gift, so have intercourse with whichever of your wives and concubines you wish, as you wish, without account, and leave intercourse with whomever of them you wish.

Others said: rather, it is from the front and back (the inverted order). The meaning of the speech is: this is Our gift without account, so grant or withhold. It is mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbd Allah: "This is Our gift, so grant or withhold; Our gift without account."

Some of the scholars of Arabic among the Basrans said regarding His saying ﴿without account﴾ that there are two meanings: first, without recompense or reward; and second, without obligation or scarcity.

The correct view in this matter is what I have mentioned from the people of interpretation, that its meaning is: he will not be called to account for what was given of that kingdom and authority. We have said that this is the correct view only because of the consensus of the authorities among the people of interpretation upon it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾:

He says: And indeed for Sulayman with Us is nearness through his turning to Us, his repentance and his obedience to Us, and a good return: He says: a good place of return and destination in the Hereafter.

As follows:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada ﴿And indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾: that is, a destination.

If someone says to us: What is the reason for Sulayman's desire toward his Lord for kingship, when he is one of the prophets, and only those of this world who prefer it over the Hereafter desire kingship? Or what is the purpose of his request, since he asked for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him, and what harm would it be if everyone after him were given the like of what was given to him? Was it stinginess on his part, so that he did not wish that kingdom to be given to whomever is given it? Or envy of people, as is mentioned from al-Ḥajjaj ibn Yusuf; for he is reported to have recited His saying ﴿And grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me﴾ and said: if it were envy, that is not among the characteristics of the prophets! It is said: as for his desire toward his Lord for what he desired of kingship, it was not, if Allah wills, a desire for this world, but a wish from him that he might know his station with Allah through His answering him in what he desired, accepting his repentance, and responding to his supplication.

As for his asking his Lord for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him, we have already mentioned earlier the saying of him who said: the meaning of that is: grant me a kingdom which I will not be stripped of as I was stripped of it before. According to those, its meaning is: grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me to strip me of it. It may also be taken to mean: that it would not befit anyone other than me among the people of my time, so that it would be a proof and a sign for me of my prophethood and that I am sent to them as Your messenger, since messengers must have signs by which they are distinguished from the rest of people. It may also be taken to mean: grant me a kingdom which You specifically reserve for me, which You give to no one but me, as an honour and dignity from You to me, to show my station with You above that of others; and none of these aspects includes what al-Ḥajjaj imagined regarding its meaning.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 36–40:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he directed﴾ [36], ﴿and the devils, every builder and diver﴾ [37], ﴿and others bound together in shackles﴾ [38], ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾ [39], ﴿and indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾ [40].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So We answered his supplication and gave him a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him. ﴿So We subjected to him the wind﴾ in place of the horses which had distracted him from prayer, ﴿running gently by his command﴾, meaning: soft and gentle, and it is from rukhawa (softness).

As follows:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Buzayʿ narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, that the Prophet of Allah Sulayman (ﷺ), when the horses were presented to him, the looking at them distracted him from the afternoon prayer ﴿until they were hidden by the veil﴾, so he became angry for the sake of Allah, and ordered them to be hamstrung, and Allah replaced them with something swifter than them: He subjected the wind, running gently by his command wherever he wished. So he would set out in the morning from Iliya, take his midday rest at Qazwin, then set out from Qazwin and spend the night at Kabul.

• I was told, from al-Ḥasan, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying ﴿And grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me﴾: he supplicated on a day when he supplicated, and he did not have the wind in his kingdom, nor every builder and diver among the devils. So he called upon his Lord at his repentance and seeking forgiveness, and Allah granted him what he asked, and his kingdom was completed.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of rukhaʾ (gentle). Some of them said regarding it something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿running gently by his command﴾ he said: good (ṭayyiba).

• al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he directed﴾, he said: swift and good; he said: not violent nor slow.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿gently﴾: rukhaʾ is the gentle one.

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAmir narrated to us, saying: Qurra narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His saying ﴿gently wherever he directed﴾, he said: not violent, nor is the moderate in between called rukhaʾ.

Others said: the meaning is: obedient to Sulayman.

Those who said that:

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying ﴿gently﴾: it means obedient to him.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿running gently by his command﴾, he said: by rukhaʾ is meant: obedient.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Nuʿman al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abu Rajaʾ, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His saying ﴿running gently by his command﴾, he said: obedient.

• I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying ﴿gently﴾: it means obedient.

• Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿gently﴾, he said: willingly.

* *

As for His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾:

It means: wherever he willed, from their saying: "Allah granted you good" (aṣāba Allāhu bika khayran), i.e., Allah willed good for you.

Interpreters said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾: it means wherever he willed.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾: wherever he willed, he settled upon it.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Nuʿman al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abu Rajaʾ, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: to wherever he willed.

• I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih ﴿wherever he directed﴾: that is, wherever he willed.

• Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We subjected the devils to him, giving him power over them in place of what We tested him with, when We cast upon his throne one of them. He used them for whatever works he willed, among them builders and divers. The builders among them made sanctuaries (maḥārīb) and statues, the divers extracted ornaments for him from the seas, and others carved for him basins and cooking pots, while the rebellious ones were bound in chains.

As follows:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾, he said: they worked for him whatever he willed of sanctuaries and statues, and divers who extracted ornaments from the sea. ﴿And others bound together in shackles﴾, he said: the rebellious devils in chains.

• I was told, from al-Maḥāribī, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾, he said: this was not in the kingdom of Dawud; Allah gave him the kingdom of Dawud and added to it the wind. ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver, and others bound together in shackles﴾, he said: meaning in chains.

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿al-asfad﴾, he said: it gathers the two hands to the neck; and al-asfad is the plural of ṣafad, which are shackles.

* *

As for His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾:

The interpreters differed concerning what is indicated by His saying ﴿this﴾ of the gift, and which gift is meant by His saying "Our gift". Some of them said: it refers to the kingdom which Allah gave him.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: al-Ḥasan said: the kingdom which We gave you; give what you wish and withhold what you wish.

• al-Maḥāribī narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak ﴿This is Our gift﴾: this is Our kingdom.

Others said: rather, it means His subjecting the devils to him, and they said: the meaning of the speech is: this which We have given you, from every builder and diver among the devils and others, is Our gift.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: these devils, imprison whomever you wish of them in your bonds and your punishment, or release whomever you wish of them, earning thereby a favour; do what you wish.

Others said: rather, it is the strength for intercourse which he had been given.

Those who said that:

• I was told, from Abu Yusuf, from Saʿid ibn Ṭarif, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Sulayman had in his loins the semen of a hundred men, and he had three hundred wives and nine hundred concubines: ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾.

The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying which we have mentioned from al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥak, that by the gift is meant the kingdom which He, may His remembrance be exalted, gave him. This is because He, may His majesty be praised, mentioned it following His report of the request of His Prophet Sulayman, peace and blessings be upon him, for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him; He informed that He subjected to him what was not subjected to any of the children of Adam, namely the wind and the devils as described. Then He, may His majesty be glorified, said to him: This which We have given you of the kingdom, and Our subjecting to you what We have subjected, is Our gift, and We have granted you what you asked Us to grant you of the kingdom that would not befit anyone after you ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾.

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of His saying ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾. Some of them said: it means: give to whomever you wish of the kingdom We have given you, and withhold from whomever you wish, there is no account upon you in that.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Ḥasan said: ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾: the kingdom which We gave you; give what you wish and withhold what you wish, there is no consequence or account upon you.

• I was told, from al-Maḥāribī, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾: he asked for a kingdom that is pleasant, not to be called to account for on the Day of Resurrection; so He said: whatever you give and whatever you withhold, there is no blame upon you.

• Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from ʿIkrima ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: give or withhold, there is no account upon you.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿so grant﴾, he said: give or withhold without account.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: free from these devils whom We subjected to you for service, or from the bonds, of those who were among them bound in shackles, whomever you wish, and imprison whomever you wish; there is no blame upon you in that.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: these devils, imprison whomever you wish of them in your bonds and your punishment, and release whomever you wish of them, earning thereby a favour; do what you wish, there is no account upon you in that.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: free from the jinn whomever you wish, and withhold whomever you wish. Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: you bestow upon whomever you wish of them, freeing him, and withhold whomever you wish, employing him; there is no account upon you in that.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: this which We have given you of the strength for intercourse is Our gift, so have intercourse with whichever of your wives and concubines you wish, as you wish, without account, and leave intercourse with whomever of them you wish.

Others said: rather, it is from the front and back (the inverted order). The meaning of the speech is: this is Our gift without account, so grant or withhold. It is mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbd Allah: "This is Our gift, so grant or withhold; Our gift without account."

Some of the scholars of Arabic among the Basrans said regarding His saying ﴿without account﴾ that there are two meanings: first, without recompense or reward; and second, without obligation or scarcity.

The correct view in this matter is what I have mentioned from the people of interpretation, that its meaning is: he will not be called to account for what was given of that kingdom and authority. We have said that this is the correct view only because of the consensus of the authorities among the people of interpretation upon it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾:

He says: And indeed for Sulayman with Us is nearness through his turning to Us, his repentance and his obedience to Us, and a good return: He says: a good place of return and destination in the Hereafter.

As follows:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada ﴿And indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾: that is, a destination.

If someone says to us: What is the reason for Sulayman's desire toward his Lord for kingship, when he is one of the prophets, and only those of this world who prefer it over the Hereafter desire kingship? Or what is the purpose of his request, since he asked for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him, and what harm would it be if everyone after him were given the like of what was given to him? Was it stinginess on his part, so that he did not wish that kingdom to be given to whomever is given it? Or envy of people, as is mentioned from al-Ḥajjaj ibn Yusuf; for he is reported to have recited His saying ﴿And grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me﴾ and said: if it were envy, that is not among the characteristics of the prophets! It is said: as for his desire toward his Lord for what he desired of kingship, it was not, if Allah wills, a desire for this world, but a wish from him that he might know his station with Allah through His answering him in what he desired, accepting his repentance, and responding to his supplication.

As for his asking his Lord for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him, we have already mentioned earlier the saying of him who said: the meaning of that is: grant me a kingdom which I will not be stripped of as I was stripped of it before. According to those, its meaning is: grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me to strip me of it. It may also be taken to mean: that it would not befit anyone other than me among the people of my time, so that it would be a proof and a sign for me of my prophethood and that I am sent to them as Your messenger, since messengers must have signs by which they are distinguished from the rest of people. It may also be taken to mean: grant me a kingdom which You specifically reserve for me, which You give to no one but me, as an honour and dignity from You to me, to show my station with You above that of others; and none of these aspects includes what al-Ḥajjaj imagined regarding its meaning.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 36–40:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he directed﴾ [36], ﴿and the devils, every builder and diver﴾ [37], ﴿and others bound together in shackles﴾ [38], ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾ [39], ﴿and indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾ [40].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So We answered his supplication and gave him a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him. ﴿So We subjected to him the wind﴾ in place of the horses which had distracted him from prayer, ﴿running gently by his command﴾, meaning: soft and gentle, and it is from rukhawa (softness).

As follows:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Buzayʿ narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, that the Prophet of Allah Sulayman (ﷺ), when the horses were presented to him, the looking at them distracted him from the afternoon prayer ﴿until they were hidden by the veil﴾, so he became angry for the sake of Allah, and ordered them to be hamstrung, and Allah replaced them with something swifter than them: He subjected the wind, running gently by his command wherever he wished. So he would set out in the morning from Iliya, take his midday rest at Qazwin, then set out from Qazwin and spend the night at Kabul.

• I was told, from al-Ḥasan, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying ﴿And grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me﴾: he supplicated on a day when he supplicated, and he did not have the wind in his kingdom, nor every builder and diver among the devils. So he called upon his Lord at his repentance and seeking forgiveness, and Allah granted him what he asked, and his kingdom was completed.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of rukhaʾ (gentle). Some of them said regarding it something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿running gently by his command﴾ he said: good (ṭayyiba).

• al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he directed﴾, he said: swift and good; he said: not violent nor slow.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿gently﴾: rukhaʾ is the gentle one.

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAmir narrated to us, saying: Qurra narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His saying ﴿gently wherever he directed﴾, he said: not violent, nor is the moderate in between called rukhaʾ.

Others said: the meaning is: obedient to Sulayman.

Those who said that:

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying ﴿gently﴾: it means obedient to him.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿running gently by his command﴾, he said: by rukhaʾ is meant: obedient.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Nuʿman al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abu Rajaʾ, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His saying ﴿running gently by his command﴾, he said: obedient.

• I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying ﴿gently﴾: it means obedient.

• Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿gently﴾, he said: willingly.

* *

As for His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾:

It means: wherever he willed, from their saying: "Allah granted you good" (aṣāba Allāhu bika khayran), i.e., Allah willed good for you.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾: wherever he willed, he settled upon it.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih ﴿wherever he directed﴾: that is, wherever he willed.

• Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

As for His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾:

The interpreters differed concerning what is indicated by His saying ﴿this﴾ of the gift, and which gift is meant by His saying "Our gift". Some of them said: it refers to the kingdom which Allah gave him.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: al-Ḥasan said: the kingdom which We gave you; give what you wish and withhold what you wish.

• al-Maḥāribī narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak ﴿This is Our gift﴾: this is Our kingdom.

Others said: rather, it means His subjecting the devils to him, and they said: the meaning of the speech is: this which We have given you, from every builder and diver among the devils and others, is Our gift.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: these devils, imprison whomever you wish of them in your bonds and your punishment, or release whomever you wish of them, earning thereby a favour; do what you wish.

Others said: rather, it is the strength for intercourse which he had been given.

Those who said that:

• I was told, from Abu Yusuf, from Saʿid ibn Ṭarif, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Sulayman had in his loins the semen of a hundred men, and he had three hundred wives and nine hundred concubines: ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾.

The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying which we have mentioned from al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥak, that by the gift is meant the kingdom which He, may His remembrance be exalted, gave him. This is because He, may His majesty be praised, mentioned it following His report of the request of His Prophet Sulayman, peace and blessings be upon him, for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him; He informed that He subjected to him what was not subjected to any of the children of Adam, namely the wind and the devils as described. Then He, may His majesty be glorified, said to him: This which We have given you of the kingdom, and Our subjecting to you what We have subjected, is Our gift, and We have granted you what you asked Us to grant you of the kingdom that would not befit anyone after you ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾.

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of His saying ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾. Some of them said: it means: give to whomever you wish of the kingdom We have given you, and withhold from whomever you wish, there is no account upon you in that.

Those who said that:
