• I was told, from al-Maḥāribī, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾: he asked for a kingdom that is pleasant, not to be called to account for on the Day of Resurrection; so He said: whatever you give and whatever you withhold, there is no blame upon you.

• Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from ʿIkrima ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: give or withhold, there is no account upon you.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿so grant﴾, he said: give or withhold without account.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: free from these devils whom We subjected to you for service, or from the bonds, of those who were among them bound in shackles, whomever you wish, and imprison whomever you wish; there is no blame upon you in that.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: these devils, imprison whomever you wish of them in your bonds and your punishment, and release whomever you wish of them, earning thereby a favour; do what you wish, there is no account upon you in that.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: free from the jinn whomever you wish, and withhold whomever you wish. Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: you bestow upon whomever you wish of them, freeing him, and withhold whomever you wish, employing him; there is no account upon you in that.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: this which We have given you of the strength for intercourse is Our gift, so have intercourse with whichever of your wives and concubines you wish, as you wish, without account, and leave intercourse with whomever of them you wish.

Others said: rather, it is from the front and back (the inverted order). The meaning of the speech is: this is Our gift without account, so grant or withhold. It is mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbd Allah: "This is Our gift, so grant or withhold; Our gift without account."

Some of the scholars of Arabic among the Basrans said regarding His saying ﴿without account﴾ that there are two meanings: first, without recompense or reward; and second, without obligation or scarcity.

The correct view in this matter is what I have mentioned from the people of interpretation, that its meaning is: he will not be called to account for what was given of that kingdom and authority. We have said that this is the correct view only because of the consensus of the authorities among the people of interpretation upon it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾:

He says: And indeed for Sulayman with Us is nearness through his turning to Us, his repentance and his obedience to Us, and a good return: He says: a good place of return and destination in the Hereafter.

As follows:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada ﴿And indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾: that is, a destination.

If someone says to us: What is the reason for Sulayman's desire toward his Lord for kingship, when he is one of the prophets, and only those of this world who prefer it over the Hereafter desire kingship? Or what is the purpose of his request, since he asked for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him, and what harm would it be if everyone after him were given the like of what was given to him? Was it stinginess on his part, so that he did not wish that kingdom to be given to whomever is given it? Or envy of people, as is mentioned from al-Ḥajjaj ibn Yusuf; for he is reported to have recited His saying ﴿And grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me﴾ and said: if it were envy, that is not among the characteristics of the prophets! It is said: as for his desire toward his Lord for what he desired of kingship, it was not, if Allah wills, a desire for this world, but a wish from him that he might know his station with Allah through His answering him in what he desired, accepting his repentance, and responding to his supplication.

As for his asking his Lord for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him, we have already mentioned earlier the saying of him who said: the meaning of that is: grant me a kingdom which I will not be stripped of as I was stripped of it before. According to those, its meaning is: grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me to strip me of it. It may also be taken to mean: that it would not befit anyone other than me among the people of my time, so that it would be a proof and a sign for me of my prophethood and that I am sent to them as Your messenger, since messengers must have signs by which they are distinguished from the rest of people. It may also be taken to mean: grant me a kingdom which You specifically reserve for me, which You give to no one but me, as an honour and dignity from You to me, to show my station with You above that of others; and none of these aspects includes what al-Ḥajjaj imagined regarding its meaning.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 36–40:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he directed﴾ [36], ﴿and the devils, every builder and diver﴾ [37], ﴿and others bound together in shackles﴾ [38], ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾ [39], ﴿and indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾ [40].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So We answered his supplication and gave him a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him. ﴿So We subjected to him the wind﴾ in place of the horses which had distracted him from prayer, ﴿running gently by his command﴾, meaning: soft and gentle, and it is from rukhawa (softness).

As follows:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Buzayʿ narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, that the Prophet of Allah Sulayman (ﷺ), when the horses were presented to him, the looking at them distracted him from the afternoon prayer ﴿until they were hidden by the veil﴾, so he became angry for the sake of Allah, and ordered them to be hamstrung, and Allah replaced them with something swifter than them: He subjected the wind, running gently by his command wherever he wished. So he would set out in the morning from Iliya, take his midday rest at Qazwin, then set out from Qazwin and spend the night at Kabul.

• I was told, from al-Ḥasan, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying ﴿And grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me﴾: he supplicated on a day when he supplicated, and he did not have the wind in his kingdom, nor every builder and diver among the devils. So he called upon his Lord at his repentance and seeking forgiveness, and Allah granted him what he asked, and his kingdom was completed.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of rukhaʾ (gentle). Some of them said regarding it something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿running gently by his command﴾ he said: good (ṭayyiba).

• al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command wherever he directed﴾, he said: swift and good; he said: not violent nor slow.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿gently﴾: rukhaʾ is the gentle one.

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAmir narrated to us, saying: Qurra narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His saying ﴿gently wherever he directed﴾, he said: not violent, nor is the moderate in between called rukhaʾ.

Others said: the meaning is: obedient to Sulayman.

Those who said that:

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying ﴿gently﴾: it means obedient to him.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿running gently by his command﴾, he said: by rukhaʾ is meant: obedient.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Nuʿman al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abu Rajaʾ, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His saying ﴿running gently by his command﴾, he said: obedient.

• I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying ﴿gently﴾: it means obedient.

• Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿gently﴾, he said: willingly.

* *

As for His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾:

It means: wherever he willed, from their saying: "Allah granted you good" (aṣāba Allāhu bika khayran), i.e., Allah willed good for you.

Interpreters said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

• ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾: it means wherever he willed.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾: wherever he willed, he settled upon it.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Nuʿman al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Abu Rajaʾ, from al-Ḥasan, concerning His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: to wherever he willed.

• I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih ﴿wherever he directed﴾: that is, wherever he willed.

• Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We subjected the devils to him, giving him power over them in place of what We tested him with, when We cast upon his throne one of them. He used them for whatever works he willed, among them builders and divers. The builders among them made sanctuaries (maḥārīb) and statues, the divers extracted ornaments for him from the seas, and others carved for him basins and cooking pots, while the rebellious ones were bound in chains.

As follows:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾, he said: they worked for him whatever he willed of sanctuaries and statues, and divers who extracted ornaments from the sea. ﴿And others bound together in shackles﴾, he said: the rebellious devils in chains.

• I was told, from al-Maḥāribī, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾, he said: this was not in the kingdom of Dawud; Allah gave him the kingdom of Dawud and added to it the wind. ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver, and others bound together in shackles﴾, he said: meaning in chains.

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿al-asfad﴾, he said: it gathers the two hands to the neck; and al-asfad is the plural of ṣafad, which are shackles.

* *

As for His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾:

The interpreters differed concerning what is indicated by His saying ﴿this﴾ of the gift, and which gift is meant by His saying "Our gift". Some of them said: it refers to the kingdom which Allah gave him.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: al-Ḥasan said: the kingdom which We gave you; give what you wish and withhold what you wish.

• al-Maḥāribī narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak ﴿This is Our gift﴾: this is Our kingdom.

Others said: rather, it means His subjecting the devils to him, and they said: the meaning of the speech is: this which We have given you, from every builder and diver among the devils and others, is Our gift.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: these devils, imprison whomever you wish of them in your bonds and your punishment, or release whomever you wish of them, earning thereby a favour; do what you wish.

Others said: rather, it is the strength for intercourse which he had been given.

Those who said that:

• I was told, from Abu Yusuf, from Saʿid ibn Ṭarif, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Sulayman had in his loins the semen of a hundred men, and he had three hundred wives and nine hundred concubines: ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾.

The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying which we have mentioned from al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥak, that by the gift is meant the kingdom which He, may His remembrance be exalted, gave him. This is because He, may His majesty be praised, mentioned it following His report of the request of His Prophet Sulayman, peace and blessings be upon him, for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him; He informed that He subjected to him what was not subjected to any of the children of Adam, namely the wind and the devils as described. Then He, may His majesty be glorified, said to him: This which We have given you of the kingdom, and Our subjecting to you what We have subjected, is Our gift, and We have granted you what you asked Us to grant you of the kingdom that would not befit anyone after you ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾.

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of His saying ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾. Some of them said: it means: give to whomever you wish of the kingdom We have given you, and withhold from whomever you wish, there is no account upon you in that.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Ḥasan said: ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾: the kingdom which We gave you; give what you wish and withhold what you wish, there is no consequence or account upon you.

• I was told, from al-Maḥāribī, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾: he asked for a kingdom that is pleasant, not to be called to account for on the Day of Resurrection; so He said: whatever you give and whatever you withhold, there is no blame upon you.

• Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from ʿIkrima ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: give or withhold, there is no account upon you.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿so grant﴾, he said: give or withhold without account.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: free from these devils whom We subjected to you for service, or from the bonds, of those who were among them bound in shackles, whomever you wish, and imprison whomever you wish; there is no blame upon you in that.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: these devils, imprison whomever you wish of them in your bonds and your punishment, and release whomever you wish of them, earning thereby a favour; do what you wish, there is no account upon you in that.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: free from the jinn whomever you wish, and withhold whomever you wish. Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: you bestow upon whomever you wish of them, freeing him, and withhold whomever you wish, employing him; there is no account upon you in that.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: this which We have given you of the strength for intercourse is Our gift, so have intercourse with whichever of your wives and concubines you wish, as you wish, without account, and leave intercourse with whomever of them you wish.

Others said: rather, it is from the front and back (the inverted order). The meaning of the speech is: this is Our gift without account, so grant or withhold. It is mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbd Allah: "This is Our gift, so grant or withhold; Our gift without account."

Some of the scholars of Arabic among the Basrans said regarding His saying ﴿without account﴾ that there are two meanings: first, without recompense or reward; and second, without obligation or scarcity.

The correct view in this matter is what I have mentioned from the people of interpretation, that its meaning is: he will not be called to account for what was given of that kingdom and authority. We have said that this is the correct view only because of the consensus of the authorities among the people of interpretation upon it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾:

He says: And indeed for Sulayman with Us is nearness through his turning to Us, his repentance and his obedience to Us, and a good return: He says: a good place of return and destination in the Hereafter.

As follows:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada ﴿And indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾: that is, a destination.

If someone says to us: What is the reason for Sulayman's desire toward his Lord for kingship, when he is one of the prophets, and only those of this world who prefer it over the Hereafter desire kingship? • Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿wherever he directed﴾, he said: wherever he willed.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We subjected the devils to him, giving him power over them in place of what We tested him with, when We cast upon his throne one of them. He used them for whatever works he willed, among them builders and divers. The builders among them made sanctuaries (maḥārīb) and statues, the divers extracted ornaments for him from the seas, and others carved for him basins and cooking pots, while the rebellious ones were bound in chains.

As follows:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾, he said: they worked for him whatever he willed of sanctuaries and statues, and divers who extracted ornaments from the sea. ﴿And others bound together in shackles﴾, he said: the rebellious devils in chains.

• I was told, from al-Maḥāribī, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾, he said: this was not in the kingdom of Dawud; Allah gave him the kingdom of Dawud and added to it the wind. ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver, and others bound together in shackles﴾, he said: meaning in chains.

• Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿al-asfad﴾, he said: it gathers the two hands to the neck; and al-asfad is the plural of ṣafad, which are shackles.

* *

As for His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾:

The interpreters differed concerning what is indicated by His saying ﴿this﴾ of the gift, and which gift is meant by His saying "Our gift". Some of them said: it refers to the kingdom which Allah gave him.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: al-Ḥasan said: the kingdom which We gave you; give what you wish and withhold what you wish.

• al-Maḥāribī narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak ﴿This is Our gift﴾: this is Our kingdom.

Others said: rather, it means His subjecting the devils to him, and they said: the meaning of the speech is: this which We have given you, from every builder and diver among the devils and others, is Our gift.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: these devils, imprison whomever you wish of them in your bonds and your punishment, or release whomever you wish of them, earning thereby a favour; do what you wish.

Others said: rather, it is the strength for intercourse which he had been given.

Those who said that:

• I was told, from Abu Yusuf, from Saʿid ibn Ṭarif, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Sulayman had in his loins the semen of a hundred men, and he had three hundred wives and nine hundred concubines: ﴿This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account﴾.

The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying which we have mentioned from al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥak, that by the gift is meant the kingdom which He, may His remembrance be exalted, gave him. This is because He, may His majesty be praised, mentioned it following His report of the request of His Prophet Sulayman, peace and blessings be upon him, for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him; He informed that He subjected to him what was not subjected to any of the children of Adam, namely the wind and the devils as described. Then He, may His majesty be glorified, said to him: This which We have given you of the kingdom, and Our subjecting to you what We have subjected, is Our gift, and We have granted you what you asked Us to grant you of the kingdom that would not befit anyone after you ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾.

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of His saying ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾. Some of them said: it means: give to whomever you wish of the kingdom We have given you, and withhold from whomever you wish, there is no account upon you in that.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Ḥasan said: ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾: the kingdom which We gave you; give what you wish and withhold what you wish, there is no consequence or account upon you.

• I was told, from al-Maḥāribī, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾: he asked for a kingdom that is pleasant, not to be called to account for on the Day of Resurrection; so He said: whatever you give and whatever you withhold, there is no blame upon you.

• Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from ʿIkrima ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: give or withhold, there is no account upon you.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Ḥarith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿so grant﴾, he said: give or withhold without account.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: free from these devils whom We subjected to you for service, or from the bonds, of those who were among them bound in shackles, whomever you wish, and imprison whomever you wish; there is no blame upon you in that.

Those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: these devils, imprison whomever you wish of them in your bonds and your punishment, and release whomever you wish of them, earning thereby a favour; do what you wish, there is no account upon you in that.

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: free from the jinn whomever you wish, and withhold whomever you wish. Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying ﴿so grant or withhold without account﴾, he said: you bestow upon whomever you wish of them, freeing him, and withhold whomever you wish, employing him; there is no account upon you in that.

Others said: rather, the meaning is: this which We have given you of the strength for intercourse is Our gift, so have intercourse with whichever of your wives and concubines you wish, as you wish, without account, and leave intercourse with whomever of them you wish.

Others said: rather, it is from the front and back (the inverted order). The meaning of the speech is: this is Our gift without account, so grant or withhold. It is mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbd Allah: "This is Our gift, so grant or withhold; Our gift without account."

Some of the scholars of Arabic among the Basrans said regarding His saying ﴿without account﴾ that there are two meanings: first, without recompense or reward; and second, without obligation or scarcity.

The correct view in this matter is what I have mentioned from the people of interpretation, that its meaning is: he will not be called to account for what was given of that kingdom and authority. We have said that this is the correct view only because of the consensus of the authorities among the people of interpretation upon it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾:

He says: And indeed for Sulayman with Us is nearness through his turning to Us, his repentance and his obedience to Us, and a good return: He says: a good place of return and destination in the Hereafter.

As follows:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada ﴿And indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾: that is, a destination.

If someone says to us: What is the reason for Sulayman's desire toward his Lord for kingship, when he is one of the prophets, and only those of this world who prefer it over the Hereafter desire kingship? Or what is the purpose of his request, since he asked for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him, and what harm would it be if everyone after him were given the like of what was given to him? Was it stinginess on his part, so that he did not wish that kingdom to be given to whomever is given it? Or envy of people, as is mentioned from al-Ḥajjaj ibn Yusuf; for he is reported to have recited His saying ﴿And grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me﴾ and said: if it were envy, that is not among the characteristics of the prophets! It is said: as for his desire toward his Lord for what he desired of kingship, it was not, if Allah wills, a desire for this world, but a wish from him that he might know his station with Allah through His answering him in what he desired, accepting his repentance, and responding to his supplication.

As for his asking his Lord for a kingdom that would not befit anyone after him, we have already mentioned earlier the saying of him who said: the meaning of that is: grant me a kingdom which I will not be stripped of as I was stripped of it before. According to those, its meaning is: grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me to strip me of it. It may also be taken to mean: that it would not befit anyone other than me among the people of my time, so that it would be a proof and a sign for me of my prophethood and that I am sent to them as Your messenger, since messengers must have signs by which they are distinguished from the rest of people. It may also be taken to mean: grant me a kingdom which You specifically reserve for me, which You give to no one but me, as an honour and dignity from You to me, to show my station with You above that of others; and none of these aspects includes what al-Ḥajjaj imagined regarding its meaning.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verses 41–42:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And remember Our servant Job, when he called upon his Lord, "Indeed, Satan has touched me with affliction and torment."﴾ [38:41] ﴿"Strike with your foot; this is a cool bath and a drink."﴾ [38:42]

Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And remember﴾ also, O Muhammad, Our servant Job, when he called upon his Lord (seeking help from Him for the trial that had befallen him): O Lord, ﴿Indeed, Satan has touched me with affliction﴾. The reciters differed concerning the reading of His saying ﴿bi-nusbin﴾. The reciters of the major cities generally read it ﴿bi-nusbin﴾ with a damma on the nun and a sukun on the sad, except Abu Ja'far al-Qari, who read it with a damma on both the nun and the sad. It has also been reported from him with a fatha on the nun and the sad. Al-Nusb and al-Nasab are equivalent to al-Huzn and al-Hazan, al-Udm and al-Adam, al-Rushd and al-Rashad, and al-Sulb and al-Salab. Al-Farra' used to say: when the first letter is pronounced with a damma, it is not made heavy, because they treated these as having two patterns: when they put a fatha on the first letter they made it heavy, and when they put a damma on the first letter they made it light. He said: some Arabs recited to me:

"If the mother of the two Humayds brings a grain-merchant... she has become rich without distress or denial" [The verse is among the evidences of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 280). He said: as for His saying "bi-nusbin wa-adhab", the reciters agreed on a damma on the nun of nusb and its lightening (i.e., the middle of the word is pronounced with a sukun), and they mentioned that Abu Ja'far al-Madani read "bi-nasbin wa-adhab" with a fatha on the nun and the sad. Both have the same meaning in tafsir. They mentioned that it means the illness and the hardship he suffered from it. Al-Nasb is equivalent to al-Huzn and al-Hazan, al-Udm and al-Udm, al-Rushd and al-Rushd, al-Sulb and al-Sulb: when it is lightened, its first letter takes a damma and it is not made heavy, because they treated them as having two patterns. When they put a fatha on the first letter, they made it heavy, and when they put a damma on it, they made it light. He said: some Arabs recited to me: "If the mother of the two Humayds..." the verse. He said: The Arabs say: jahada 'aysahum juhdan, meaning when it became narrow and severe. When he said juhd, and put a damma on its first letter, he lightened it. Build on this what you have seen of these two dialects. End of quotation. I say: al-Ma'ir is the one who brings provisions.]]

From their saying: jahida 'aysuhu, meaning when it became narrow and severe. He said: when he said juhd, he lightened it.

Some of the scholars of Arabic speech among the Basrans said: al-Nasub is from torment. He said: the Arabs say: anṣabanī, meaning he tormented me and afflicted me. He said: some of them say nasabanī, and he cited for this saying the verse of Bishr ibn Abi Khazim:

"Weariness of [love for] Umayma has wearied you, as one with grief who has not yet been relieved and will not be relieved..." [The verse is by Bishr ibn Abi Hazim (Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda, folio 215). He said: "bi-nusbin wa-adhab": Bishr ibn Abi Hazim said "...the verse". And al-Nabigha said: "Leave me to them, O Umayma, one who is wearied... the verse." Then after the two verses he said: The Arabs say: anṣabanī, meaning he tormented me and afflicted me. Some of them say nasabanī. Al-Nasb, when its letters are pronounced with fatha and movement, is from fatigue. Al-Nasb when its first letter has fatha and its second is sukun is the singular of anṣab al-haram (the stones of the sacred precinct), and everything you set up and make a sign. It is said: la-ansabanna laka nasb al-'ud (I will certainly set you up like a stick).]]

He said: By al-Nasb he means affliction and evil. From it is the saying of al-Nabigha of the Banu Dhubyan:

"Leave me, O Umayma, to a worry that wearies, and to a night I endure, slow in its stars..." [The verse is by al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa, Halabi edition, p. 159). Its commentator said: kilini means da'ini (leave me). Umayma with fatha (and the better is with damma) is a vocative. Al-Khalil said: it is the custom of the Arabs to address the feminine by apocope (tarkhim), and when it is not apocopated here (because of the meter), he left it in its full form, and gave it a fatha. Nasib means wearying. Batī' al-kawākib means its stars do not set, and it is a metaphor for length, because the poet was anxious. End of quotation. The verse has been mentioned earlier in the explanation of the previous evidence, from Abu 'Ubayda, because the place of evidence in both is shared.]]

⁕ Bishr ibn Adam narrated to me, saying: Abu Qutayba narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan, concerning God's saying: ﴿Strike with your foot﴾; so he struck with his foot, and a spring gushed forth, and he bathed in it. Then he walked about forty cubits, then he struck with his foot, and a spring gushed forth, and he drank from it. That is His saying: ﴿Strike with your foot; this is a cool bath and a drink.﴾

By His saying ﴿mughtasal﴾ he means the water with which one bathes. It is said of it: hadha mughtasal, and ghasul, for that by which one bathes with water.

* *

As for His saying ﴿wa-sharab﴾

It means: and he drinks from it. The place where one bathes is called a mughtasal.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 43–44:

The interpretation of His words, "And We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding" (38:43), and "And take in your hand a bundle, and strike with it and do not break your oath. Indeed, We found him patient; an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back [to Allah]" (38:44).

The interpreters of the Qur'an differed concerning the meaning of His words, "And We gave him his family and the like of them with them." We have mentioned their differences on this and the correct view in our opinion concerning it in Surah al-Anbiya', so there is no need to repeat it in this place. The meaning of the speech is: he washed and drank, and We relieved him of the affliction he was in, and We gave him his family, from wife and child, "and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us," to him and compassion, "and a reminder," meaning: and a reminder to people of intellect, so that they may take heed from it and be admonished.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Prophet of Allah, Ayyub, remained in his affliction for eighteen years. Both the near and the far abandoned him, except for two men from among his brothers who were among his closest brothers to him. They would come to him in the morning and in the evening. One of them said to his companion: 'You know, by Allah, Ayyub has committed a sin the like of which no one among the worlds has committed.' His companion said to him: 'And what is that?' He said: 'For eighteen years Allah has not had mercy on him so as to remove what is upon him.' When they came to him, the man could not restrain himself until he mentioned that to him. Ayyub said: 'I do not know what you are saying, except that Allah knows that I used to pass by two men who were quarreling and they mentioned Allah, so I would return to my house and atone on their behalf, out of dislike that Allah be mentioned except in what is right.' He said: And he used to go out for his need, and when he finished it, his wife would hold his hand until he reached [home]. One day he was late to her, and it was revealed to Ayyub in his place: 'Strike the earth with your foot; this is a cool washing-place and a drink' (38:42). She was slow to him, so she came out to meet him looking [for him], and he approached her, Allah having removed from him the affliction he had, and he was in the best state he had been in. When she saw him she said: 'May Allah bless you, have you seen the Prophet of Allah, this afflicted one? By Allah, I have not seen anyone more resembling him than you when he was healthy.' He said: 'Indeed, I am he.' He said: And he had two threshing-floors: a threshing-floor for wheat and a threshing-floor for barley. Allah sent two clouds, and when one of them was over the threshing-floor of wheat, it poured gold into it until it overflowed, and the other poured silver into the threshing-floor of barley until it overflowed."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning "And We gave him his family and the like of them with them," he said: Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Allah revived them with their same persons and increased them with the like of them.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Awf narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, saying: Safwan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to us, saying: When the Prophet of Allah Ayyub (ﷺ) was tested in his wealth, his children and his body, and was cast onto a dunghill, his wife began to go out and earn for him what they would feed him. Satan envied her for that, and he would come to the people of the bread and roasted meat who used to give her charity, and say: "Drive away this woman who comes to you, for she tends to her companion and touches him with her hand, so people find your food repulsive because she comes to you and approaches you for that reason." When she went out, he would meet her looking grieved for what Ayyub had suffered, and say: "Your companion persists; he refuses except what has come upon him. By Allah, if he spoke one word, every harm would be lifted from him, and his wealth and children would be returned to him." So she would come and inform Ayyub, and he would say to her: "The enemy of Allah met you and taught you these words. Woe to you! Your likeness is only that of the adulterous woman: when her lover brings something, she accepts him and lets him in, and if he does not bring anything, she drives him away and shuts her door on him! When Allah gave us wealth and children, we believed in Him, and when He takes back what is His from us, we disbelieve in Him and substitute others for Him! If Allah restores me from this illness of mine, I will surely flog you a hundred times." He said: So for that Allah said: "And take in your hand a bundle, and strike with it and do not break your oath."

And His words, "And take in your hand a bundle" (ḍighth):

He says: And We said to Ayyub: Take in your hand a bundle (ḍighth), which is what is gathered of something, like a bundle of fresh clover, or a handful of trees or grass, and the flower-stalks and the like, of whatever stands on a stalk. From it is the saying of 'Awf ibn al-Khari':

"And beneath me a robust mare I have tethered, and I cast a bundle of green fresh grass..."

[[The verse is by 'Awf ibn al-Kharia (Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah, p. 215 b). In the Mu'jam al-Shu'ara' it is confirmed as 'Awf ibn 'Atiyyah ibn al-Kharia, and likewise in al-Taj. Abu 'Ubaydah said when interpreting His words, "And take in your hand a bundle (ḍighth)": it is a handful of trees or grass, flower-stalks and the like, and quoted 'Awf ibn al-Kharia: "And beneath me..." (the verse). In al-Lisan: a "nahd" horse is a large, noble, strong one, and the feminine is nahdah; "khala" is fresh grass (like clover, or it is clover).]]

Al-Tabari said: The interpreters said according to what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said so:

⁕ 'Ali narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words, "And take in your hand a bundle (ḍighth)," he says: a bundle (ḥuzmah).

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words, "And take in your hand a bundle, and strike with it and do not break your oath," he said: He was commanded to take a bundle of fresh twigs equal to what he had sworn to, and strike with it.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', concerning His words, "And take in your hand a bundle," he said: fresh sticks.

⁕ Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from his father, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, "And take in your hand a bundle," he said: It is the tamarisk (athl).

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, "And take in your hand a bundle..." to the end of the verse, he said: His wife had made an overture to him in a matter, and Iblis had urged him toward something, saying: "If you spoke such and such a thing..." and it was only despair that moved her to it. So the Prophet of Allah swore: "If Allah cures me, I will surely flog her a hundred lashes." He said: So he was commanded with a branch containing ninety-nine twigs, and the root of it was to complete the hundred, so he struck her with one blow, and the Prophet of Allah fulfilled his oath, and Allah lightened [the burden] for His servant, and Allah is Merciful.

⁕ I was told by al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words, "And take in your hand a bundle," meaning a bundle of fresh trees, that he had sworn an oath, so he took from the trees a number equal to what he had sworn to, and struck with it one blow, and his oath was fulfilled. And it is today among the people the "oath of Ayyub"; whoever acts upon it, it is good.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words, "And take in your hand a bundle, and strike with it and do not break your oath," he said: one bundle of herbage in which there were more than a hundred stalks, and he struck with it one blow, and that is a hundred blows.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Awf narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, saying: Safwan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to us, concerning "And take in your hand a bundle, and strike with it," he says: strike your wife with the bundle, so that you fulfil the oath you swore that you would strike her, "and do not break your oath," he says: and do not break your oath.

* *

And His words, "Indeed, We found him patient; an excellent servant":

He says: Indeed, We found Ayyub patient over the affliction, not that the affliction moved him to depart from the obedience of Allah and enter into His disobedience, "an excellent servant, indeed he was one who repeatedly turned back," he says: indeed he was turned toward the obedience of Allah, and returning often to His pleasure.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 43–44:

The interpretation of His words, "And We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding" (38:43), and "And take in your hand a bundle, and strike with it and do not break your oath. Indeed, We found him patient; an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back [to Allah]" (38:44).

The interpreters of the Qur'an differed concerning the meaning of His words, "And We gave him his family and the like of them with them." We have mentioned their differences on this and the correct view in our opinion concerning it in Surah al-Anbiya', so there is no need to repeat it in this place. The meaning of the speech is: he washed and drank, and We relieved him of the affliction he was in, and We gave him his family, from wife and child, "and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us," to him and compassion, "and a reminder," meaning: and a reminder to people of intellect, so that they may take heed from it and be admonished.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Prophet of Allah, Ayyub, remained in his affliction for eighteen years. Both the near and the far abandoned him, except for two men from among his brothers who were among his closest brothers to him. They would come to him in the morning and in the evening. One of them said to his companion: 'You know, by Allah, Ayyub has committed a sin the like of which no one among the worlds has committed.' His companion said to him: 'And what is that?' He said: 'For eighteen years Allah has not had mercy on him so as to remove what is upon him.' When they came to him, the man could not restrain himself until he mentioned that to him. Ayyub said: 'I do not know what you are saying, except that Allah knows that I used to pass by two men who were quarreling and they mentioned Allah, so I would return to my house and atone on their behalf, out of dislike that Allah be mentioned except in what is right.' He said: And he used to go out for his need, and when he finished it, his wife would hold his hand until he reached [home]. One day he was late to her, and it was revealed to Ayyub in his place: 'Strike the earth with your foot; this is a cool washing-place and a drink' (38:42). She was slow to him, so she came out to meet him looking [for him], and he approached her, Allah having removed from him the affliction he had, and he was in the best state he had been in. When she saw him she said: 'May Allah bless you, have you seen the Prophet of Allah, this afflicted one? By Allah, I have not seen anyone more resembling him than you when he was healthy.' He said: 'Indeed, I am he.' He said: And he had two threshing-floors: a threshing-floor for wheat and a threshing-floor for barley. Allah sent two clouds, and when one of them was over the threshing-floor of wheat, it poured gold into it until it overflowed, and the other poured silver into the threshing-floor of barley until it overflowed."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning "And We gave him his family and the like of them with them," he said: Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Allah revived them with their same persons and increased them with the like of them.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Awf narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, saying: Safwan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to us, saying: When the Prophet of Allah Ayyub (ﷺ) was tested in his wealth, his children and his body, and was cast onto a dunghill, his wife began to go out and earn for him what they would feed him. Satan envied her for that, and he would come to the people of the bread and roasted meat who used to give her charity, and say: "Drive away this woman who comes to you, for she tends to her companion and touches him with her hand, so people find your food repulsive because she comes to you and approaches you for that reason." When she went out, he would meet her looking grieved for what Ayyub had suffered, and say: "Your companion persists; he refuses except what has come upon him. By Allah, if he spoke one word, every harm would be lifted from him, and his wealth and children would be returned to him." So she would come and inform Ayyub, and he would say to her: "The enemy of Allah met you and taught you these words. Woe to you! Your likeness is only that of the adulterous woman: when her lover brings something, she accepts him and lets him in, and if he does not bring anything, she drives him away and shuts her door on him! When Allah gave us wealth and children, we believed in Him, and when He takes back what is His from us, we disbelieve in Him and substitute others for Him! If Allah restores me from this illness of mine, I will surely flog you a hundred times." He said: So for that Allah said: "And take in your hand a bundle, and strike with it and do not break your oath."

And His words, "And take in your hand a bundle" (ḍighth):

He says: And We said to Ayyub: Take in your hand a bundle (ḍighth), which is what is gathered of something, like a bundle of fresh clover, or a handful of trees or grass, and the flower-stalks and the like, of whatever stands on a stalk. From it is the saying of 'Awf ibn al-Khari':

"And beneath me a robust mare I have tethered, and I cast a bundle of green fresh grass..."

[[The verse is by 'Awf ibn al-Kharia (Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah, p. 215 b). In the Mu'jam al-Shu'ara' it is confirmed as 'Awf ibn 'Atiyyah ibn al-Kharia, and likewise in al-Taj. Abu 'Ubaydah said when interpreting His words, "And take in your hand a bundle (ḍighth)": it is a handful of trees or grass, flower-stalks and the like, and quoted 'Awf ibn al-Kharia: "And beneath me..." (the verse). In al-Lisan: a "nahd" horse is a large, noble, strong one, and the feminine is nahdah; "khala" is fresh grass (like clover, or it is clover).]]

Al-Tabari said: The interpreters said according to what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said so:

* *

And His words, "Indeed, We found him patient; an excellent servant":

He says: Indeed, We found Ayyub patient over the affliction, not that the affliction moved him to depart from the obedience of Allah and enter into His disobedience, "an excellent servant, indeed he was one who repeatedly turned back," he says: indeed he was turned toward the obedience of Allah, and returning often to His pleasure.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, possessors of strength and vision.﴾ (45) ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Home.﴾ (46) ﴿And indeed they are with Us among the chosen and the excellent.﴾ (47)

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying ﴿ʿibādanā﴾ (our servants). The majority of the reciters of the metropolitan cities read ﴿wa-dhkur ʿibādanā﴾ in the plural, except Ibn Kathir, from whom it is reported that he read "wa-dhkur ʿabdanā" (in the singular), as though he directed the speech to the effect that Isaac and Jacob are from the offspring of Abraham and were mentioned after him.

Ḥadīth: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās recite: "wa-dhkur ʿabdanā inna Ibrāhīm," and he said: "Only Abraham is mentioned, then his offspring were mentioned after him."

The correct reading in this matter, in his view, is the reading of those who read it in the plural, on the basis that Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are an explanation of and an apposition to the "servants," because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿possessors of strength and vision﴾:

By "the hands" is meant strength; he says: those possessed of strength in worshipping God and obeying Him. By "the visions" is meant that they possessed the vision of the hearts, meaning: possessors of intellects [[The phrase may have dropped a word from them both, "wa-l-abṣār" (and the visions), as is understood from what precedes it and what follows.]] for the truth.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of this, and some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Ḥadīth: ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿possessors of hands﴾: he says: possessors of strength and worship; and "al-abṣār" he says: understanding in religion.

Ḥadīth: Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿possessors of hands and vision﴾: he said: they were distinguished by strength and worship.

Ḥadīth: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Manṣūr, that he said regarding this verse, ﴿possessors of hands﴾: strength.

Ḥadīth: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥakkām narrated to us, from ʿAnbasa, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from al-Qāsim ibn Abī Bazza, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿possessors of hands﴾: strength in the command of God.

Ḥadīth: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥakkām narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, ﴿possessors of hands﴾: he said: "the hands": strength in the command of God; "and the visions": the intellects.

Ḥadīth: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, ﴿possessors of hands and vision﴾: he said: strength in obedience to God, and "the vision": the sight in the truth.

Ḥadīth: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, regarding His saying ﴿possessors of hands and vision﴾, he says: they were given strength in worship and vision in religion.

Ḥadīth: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding His saying ﴿possessors of hands and vision﴾: he said: "the hands": strength in obedience to God; "and the vision": the sight by their intellects in their religion.

Ḥadīth: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿possessors of hands and vision﴾: he said: "the hands": strength; "and the vision": the intellects.

If someone says to us: how are "hands" strength, when "hands" is merely the plural of "hand," and the hand is a limb, and how are "intellects" "visions," when "visions" is the plural of "sight"? It is said: this is a figure of speech, since with the hand one seizes, and by seizing the strength of the strong is known; therefore the strong is called "one who has a hand." As for "sight," it means the sight of the heart, and by it the knowledge of things is attained; therefore a man who knows a thing is said to "see" it. It is also possible that by His saying ﴿possessors of hands﴾ He meant: those who have hands with God through righteous deeds, so God made their righteous deeds which they performed in the world into "hands" for them with God, a figure drawn from the hand that is held by another man.

It is reported from ʿAbd Allāh that he used to read it: "awlā al-Aydi," without a yāʾ, and it may be that this is from "taʾyīd" (support), and that it means "al-Aydi," but the yāʾ was dropped from it, as in the saying: ﴿the Day the caller calls﴾; and His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality﴾ means: exalted is His remembrance: We singled them out with a specific quality: the remembrance of the Home.

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying ﴿with a pure quality, the remembrance of the Home﴾. The majority of the reciters of Madina read "bi-khāliṣati dhikrā al-dār" with the genitive construction, joining "khāliṣa" to "dhikrā al-dār," meaning: they were purified by the pure remembrance; and "the remembrance," when read this way, is other than the "pure," just as "al-mutakabbir" (the arrogant), when read "ʿalā kulli qalbin mutakabbir" (upon every heart of an arrogant one) with the genitive joining "qalb" to "mutakabbir," is the one who possesses the heart, not the heart itself. And the majority of the reciters of Iraq read ﴿bi-khāliṣatin dhikrā al-dār﴾ with tanwīn on "khāliṣatan" and with "dhikrā" as its complement, on the basis that the Home itself is the pure one; so they made "the remembrance," which is definite, a complement of "khāliṣa," which is indefinite, as in the saying: "li-sharri maʾāb: jahannam" (for the evil place of return: Hell), where "Jahannam," which is definite, is made an apposition to "maʾāb," which is indefinite.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that these are two readings widely transmitted among the reciters of the cities, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: We purified them with a pure quality which is the remembrance of the Home, that is, they used to remind people of the Hereafter and call them to obedience to God and to work for the Hereafter.

Those who said that:

Ḥadīth: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Home﴾, he said: by this God purified them; they used to call to the Hereafter and to God.

Others said: the meaning of that is that He purified them by their work for the Hereafter and their remembrance of it.

Those who said that:

Ḥadīth: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Azdī narrated to me, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Yamān narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Home﴾, he said: by the remembrance of the Hereafter, for they had no concern other than it.

Ḥadīth: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Home﴾, he said: by their remembrance of the Home of the Hereafter and their work for the Hereafter.

Others said: the meaning of that is: We purified them with the best of what is in the Hereafter; and this interpretation is upon the reading of the one who read it with the genitive construction. As for the first two opinions, they are upon the interpretation of the reading of the one who read it with tanwīn.

Those who said that:

Ḥadīth: Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying "Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality, the remembrance of the Home": with the best of what is in the Hereafter We purified them, and We gave it to them; he said: and "the Home" is Paradise, and he recited: ﴿That is the Last Abode, which We assign to those who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth﴾, he said: it is Paradise; and he recited: ﴿and how excellent is the home of the righteous﴾, he said: all of this is Paradise; and he said: We purified them with the good of the Hereafter.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: a pure outcome of the Home.

Those who said that:

Ḥadīth: Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sharīk, from Sālim al-Afṭas, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿with a pure quality, the remembrance of the Home﴾, he said: "ʿuqbā al-dār" (the final outcome of the Home).

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: with the pure ones of the people of the Home.

Those who said that:

It was related to me from Ibn Abī Zāʾida, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abī Najīḥ told me that he heard Mujāhid say: ﴿with a pure quality, the remembrance of the Home﴾: they are the people of the Home; and "dhū al-dār" (possessor of the Home) is like your saying "dhū al-Kalāʿ" and "dhū Yazan."

Some scholars of the Arabic language among the Basrans used to interpret this according to the reading with tanwīn, that "bi-khāliṣatin" is governed by the remembrance of the Hereafter.

The most correct of the statements regarding this, according to the reading of the one who read it with tanwīn, is to say: its meaning is: We purified them with a pure quality, which is the remembrance of the Abode of the Hereafter, so they worked for it in the world, obeying God and being mindful of Him; and it may enter into their description that among their attributes is also calling to God and to the Abode of the Hereafter, since that is part of obedience to God and work for the Hereafter, though the meaning of the word is what I have mentioned. As for the reading of the one who read it with the genitive construction, it is to be said: its meaning is: We purified them with a pure quality of what is mentioned concerning the Abode of the Hereafter; and since "fī" (in) was not mentioned, the "remembrance" was made to be genitive to "the Home," as we have already explained before concerning His saying ﴿man does not tire of asking for good﴾ and His saying ﴿with the request of your ewe for his ewes﴾.

His saying ﴿And indeed they are with Us among the chosen and the excellent﴾:

He says: And indeed these whom We have mentioned are with Us among those whom We chose for the remembrance of the Hereafter, the excellent, whom We selected for Our obedience and for Our messages to Our creation.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, possessors of strength and vision.﴾ (45) ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Home.﴾ (46) ﴿And indeed they are with Us among the chosen and the excellent.﴾ (47)

Ḥadīth: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥakkām narrated to us, from ʿAnbasa, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from al-Qāsim ibn Abī Bazza, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿possessors of hands﴾: strength in the command of God.

Ḥadīth: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥakkām narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, ﴿possessors of hands﴾: he said: "the hands": strength in the command of God; "and the visions": the intellects.

Ḥadīth: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, ﴿possessors of hands and vision﴾: he said: strength in obedience to God, and "the vision": the sight in the truth.

Ḥadīth: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, regarding His saying ﴿possessors of hands and vision﴾, he says: they were given strength in worship and vision in religion.

Ḥadīth: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding His saying ﴿possessors of hands and vision﴾: he said: "the hands": strength in obedience to God; "and the vision": the sight by their intellects in their religion.

Ḥadīth: Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿possessors of hands and vision﴾: he said: "the hands": strength; "and the vision": the intellects.

If someone says to us: how are "hands" strength, when "hands" is merely the plural of "hand," and the hand is a limb, and how are "intellects" "visions," when "visions" is the plural of "sight"? It is said: this is a figure of speech, since with the hand one seizes, and by seizing the strength of the strong is known; therefore the strong is called "one who has a hand." As for "sight," it means the sight of the heart, and by it the knowledge of things is attained; therefore a man who knows a thing is said to "see" it. It is also possible that by His saying ﴿possessors of hands﴾ He meant: those who have hands with God through righteous deeds, so God made their righteous deeds which they performed in the world into "hands" for them with God, a figure drawn from the hand that is held by another man.

It is reported from ʿAbd Allāh that he used to read it: "awlā al-Aydi," without a yāʾ, and it may be that this is from "taʾyīd" (support), and that it means "al-Aydi," but the yāʾ was dropped from it, as in the saying: ﴿the Day the caller calls﴾; and His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality﴾ means: exalted is His remembrance: We singled them out with a specific quality: the remembrance of the Home.

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying ﴿with a pure quality, the remembrance of the Home﴾. The majority of the reciters of Madina read "bi-khāliṣati dhikrā al-dār" with the genitive construction, joining "khāliṣa" to "dhikrā al-dār," meaning: they were purified by the pure remembrance; and "the remembrance," when read this way, is other than the "pure," just as "al-mutakabbir" (the arrogant), when read "ʿalā kulli qalbin mutakabbir" (upon every heart of an arrogant one) with the genitive joining "qalb" to "mutakabbir," is the one who possesses the heart, not the heart itself. And the majority of the reciters of Iraq read ﴿bi-khāliṣatin dhikrā al-dār﴾ with tanwīn on "khāliṣatan" and with "dhikrā" as its complement, on the basis that the Home itself is the pure one; so they made "the remembrance," which is definite, a complement of "khāliṣa," which is indefinite, as in the saying: "li-sharri maʾāb: jahannam" (for the evil place of return: Hell), where "Jahannam," which is definite, is made an apposition to "maʾāb," which is indefinite.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that these are two readings widely transmitted among the reciters of the cities, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: We purified them with a pure quality which is the remembrance of the Home, that is, they used to remind people of the Hereafter and call them to obedience to God and to work for the Hereafter.

Those who said that:

Ḥadīth: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Home﴾, he said: by this God purified them; they used to call to the Hereafter and to God.

Others said: the meaning of that is that He purified them by their work for the Hereafter and their remembrance of it.

Those who said that:

Ḥadīth: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Azdī narrated to me, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Yamān narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Home﴾, he said: by the remembrance of the Hereafter, for they had no concern other than it.

Ḥadīth: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Home﴾, he said: by their remembrance of the Home of the Hereafter and their work for the Hereafter.

Others said: the meaning of that is: We purified them with the best of what is in the Hereafter; and this interpretation is upon the reading of the one who read it with the genitive construction. As for the first two opinions, they are upon the interpretation of the reading of the one who read it with tanwīn.

Those who said that:

Ḥadīth: Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying "Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality, the remembrance of the Home": with the best of what is in the Hereafter We purified them, and We gave it to them; he said: and "the Home" is Paradise, and he recited: ﴿That is the Last Abode, which We assign to those who do not desire haughtiness upon the earth﴾, he said: it is Paradise; and he recited: ﴿and how excellent is the home of the righteous﴾, he said: all of this is Paradise; and he said: We purified them with the good of the Hereafter.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: a pure outcome of the Home.

Those who said that:

Ḥadīth: Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sharīk, from Sālim al-Afṭas, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿with a pure quality, the remembrance of the Home﴾, he said: "ʿuqbā al-dār" (the final outcome of the Home).

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: with the pure ones of the people of the Home.

Those who said that:

It was related to me from Ibn Abī Zāʾida, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abī Najīḥ told me that he heard Mujāhid say: ﴿with a pure quality, the remembrance of the Home﴾: they are the people of the Home; and "dhū al-dār" (possessor of the Home) is like your saying "dhū al-Kalāʿ" and "dhū Yazan."

Some scholars of the Arabic language among the Basrans used to interpret this according to the reading with tanwīn, that "bi-khāliṣatin" is governed by the remembrance of the Hereafter.

The most correct of the statements regarding this, according to the reading of the one who read it with tanwīn, is to say: its meaning is: We purified them with a pure quality, which is the remembrance of the Abode of the Hereafter, so they worked for it in the world, obeying God and being mindful of Him; and it may enter into their description that among their attributes is also calling to God and to the Abode of the Hereafter, since that is part of obedience to God and work for the Hereafter, though the meaning of the word is what I have mentioned. As for the reading of the one who read it with the genitive construction, it is to be said: its meaning is: We purified them with a pure quality of what is mentioned concerning the Abode of the Hereafter; and since "fī" (in) was not mentioned, the "remembrance" was made to be genitive to "the Home," as we have already explained before concerning His saying ﴿man does not tire of asking for good﴾ and His saying ﴿with the request of your ewe for his ewes﴾.

His saying ﴿And indeed they are with Us among the chosen and the excellent﴾:

He says: And indeed these whom We have mentioned are with Us among those whom We chose for the remembrance of the Hereafter, the excellent, whom We selected for Our obedience and for Our messages to Our creation.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, possessors of strength and vision.﴾ (45) ﴿Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Home.﴾ (46) ﴿And indeed they are with Us among the chosen and the excellent.﴾ (47)

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying ﴿ʿibādanā﴾ (our servants). The majority of the reciters of the metropolitan cities read ﴿wa-dhkur ʿibādanā﴾ in the plural, except Ibn Kathir, from whom it is reported that he read "wa-dhkur ʿabdanā" (in the singular), as though he directed the speech to the effect that Isaac and Jacob are from the offspring of Abraham and were mentioned after him.

Ḥadīth: Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās recite: "wa-dhkur ʿabdanā inna Ibrāhīm," and he said: "Only Abraham is mentioned, then his offspring were mentioned after him."

The correct reading in this matter, in his view, is the reading of those who read it in the plural, on the basis that Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are an explanation of and an apposition to the "servants," because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿possessors of strength and vision﴾:

By "the hands" is meant strength; he says: those possessed of strength in worshipping God and obeying Him. By "the visions" is meant that they possessed the vision of the hearts, meaning: possessors of intellects [[The phrase may have dropped a word from them both, "wa-l-abṣār" (and the visions), as is understood from what precedes it and what follows.]] for the truth.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of this, and some of them said something similar to what we have said.

His saying ﴿And indeed they are with Us among the chosen and the excellent﴾:

He says: And indeed these whom We have mentioned are with Us among those whom We chose for the remembrance of the Hereafter, the excellent, whom We selected for Our obedience and for Our messages to Our creation.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 48–49:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And remember Ismail, al-Yasa' and Dhu l-Kifl, and each is among the chosen ones﴾ (48) ﴿This is a reminder. And indeed, for the God-fearing is a good place of return﴾ (49)

Says God, the Exalted, to His Prophet (ﷺ): "And remember, O Muhammad, Ismail, al-Yasa' and Dhu l-Kifl, and what they achieved in obedience to God, so follow their example and tread their path in patience over what befalls you for God's sake, and in persevering to convey His message." We have already explained earlier in this book of ours, from the accounts of Ismail, al-Yasa' and Dhu l-Kifl, what makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. And al-kifl (الكِفْل) in the speech of the Arabs means a share and good fortune (الحظّ والجَدّ).

* *

As for His saying ﴿This is a reminder﴾:

Says God, the Exalted: "This Qur'an which We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, is a reminder for you and your people; We have made you and them mindful of it."

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

Whoever said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿This is a reminder﴾, he said: "The Qur'an."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, for the God-fearing is a good place of return﴾

Meaning: And indeed, for those who are God-fearing, who have feared Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, there is a good place of return to which they return in the Hereafter, and a destination to which they arrive. Then God, the Exalted, informed about what that good place of return He promised is, saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, whose doors are opened for them﴾.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿And indeed, for the God-fearing is a good place of return﴾, he said: "A good place of return."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verses 50–51:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Gardens of perpetual abode, their gates opened for them﴾ (50) ﴿reclining therein, calling therein for abundant fruit and drink﴾ (51).

His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Gardens of perpetual abode﴾ are an explanation of the good place of return, and a rendering of it. Its meaning: gardens of abiding residence. We have already clarified the meaning of this with its evidences, and mentioned the differences of opinion concerning it in what has passed, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary.

Bishr has narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Gardens of perpetual abode﴾, he said: Umar asked Ka'b (about) "'Adn", what is it? He said: O Commander of the Faithful, they are palaces in Paradise of gold, which the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the leaders of justice will dwell in.

* *

And His words ﴿their gates opened for them﴾.

He means: their gates are opened for them. The alif and lam were placed upon "al-abwab" (the gates) in place of the possessive construction, as it was said: ﴿Indeed Paradise is the refuge﴾, meaning: it is his refuge, and as the poet said:

"Hayyah, the daughter of Malik, did not bear you in fornication, nor were her words lying tales,
But we see our feet in your sandals, and our noses between your beards and your eyebrows."

[[The two verses are cited by al-Farra in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 281) as evidence that His words "mufattahatan lahumu al-abwab" are with the nominative "al-abwab", because the meaning is "its gates opened for them". The Arabs make the alif and lam a substitute for the possessive, and from this is His words "indeed Hellfire is the refuge", meaning, God knows best: its refuge. Similar is the poet's saying: "What bore you was not a Rabi'i woman..." the two verses. Its meaning: "and we see our noses between your jaws and eyebrows in resemblance." End quote. Hayyah bint Malik: a tribe. Sifah: fornication. Al-luha: plural of lihyah.]]

That is: between your beards and eyebrows. Had "al-abwab" come in the accusative, it would not have been an error, and its accusative would be by directing "mufattahah" in wording to "jannat", though in meaning it refers to "al-abwab", as in the poet's saying:

"My people are not of Tha'labah ibn Sa'd, nor of Fazarah, the hairy-necked ones (al-sha'r al-raqaba)."

"Hayyah, the daughter of Malik, did not bear you in fornication, nor were her words lying tales,
But we see our feet in your sandals, and our noses between your beards and your eyebrows."
