(See the commentary on the evidences of al-Shafiya by al-Radi, p. 497).]]

The nominative is by the ha' in His words ﴿so let them taste it﴾, as one says: "the night, so hasten to it," and "the night, so hasten to it" (with the nominative).

* As narrated by Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿This! So let them taste it: scalding water and ghassāq﴾, he said: "Ḥamīm: that whose heat has reached its extreme."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Ḥamīm is the tears of their eyes, gathered in the pools of the Fire, and they are given to drink from it."

* *

His words ﴿and ghassāq﴾

The reciters differed in its recitation. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz, Basra, some of Kufa and Syria recited it with lightening: "wa-ghasāq," and said: it is a noun established as such. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it with the doubled sin: ﴿wa-ghassāq﴾, and directed it to being an attributive noun from their saying: ghasaqa yaghsiqu ghusūqan, when it flowed, and they said: its meaning is that they are given scalding water and what flows from their pus.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that they are two recitations, and that scholars among the reciters have recited each of them, so whichever of the two a reciter recites is correct; though the doubling of the sin is more complete in our view, because it is the known usage in speech, while the other is not rejected as sound.

The interpreters differed on the meaning of this. Some of them said: it is what flows from their skins of pus and blood.

Those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿This! So let them taste it: scalding water and ghassāq﴾, he said: "We used to narrate that ghassāq is what flows from between their skin and flesh."

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "Ghassāq is what flows from their eyes of their tears, which they are given to drink with the scalding water."

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: "Ghassāq is what flows from their eye-discharge and what drops from their skins."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Ghassāq: the pus which is collected from their skins, which the Fire melts in pools where it gathers, and they are given to drink it."

* Yahya ibn Uthman ibn Salih al-Sahmi narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, saying: Abu Qabil narrated to me that he heard Abu Hubayra al-Ziyadi say: I heard Abd Allah ibn Amr say: "What is ghassāq?" They said: "God knows best." Abd Allah ibn Amr said: "It is thick pus; if a drop of it were poured out in the west, it would stink the people of the east, and if it were poured out in the east, it would stink the people of the west."

Yahya ibn Uthman said, my father said: Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us again, saying: Abu Qabil narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Hubayra, and he did not mention Abu Hubayra to us.

* Ibn Awf narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: Safwan narrated to us, saying: Abu Yahya Atiyya al-Kala'i narrated to us, that Ka'b used to say: "Do you know what ghassāq is?" They said: "No, by God." He said: "A spring in Hell, into which flows the venom of every venomous creature, a snake or a scorpion or others, and it stagnates, and a human is brought and dipped in it once, and he comes out with his skin and flesh fallen from the bones, until his skin hangs at his ankles and heels, and his flesh is dragged as a man drags his garment."

Others said: it is the cold which cannot be endured because of its coldness.

Those who said this:

* I was told by Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and ghassāq﴾, he said: "Cold that cannot be endured," or he said: "Cold that cannot be endured."

* Ali ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿This! So let them taste it: scalding water and ghassāq﴾, he said: "It is said: ghassāq is the most extreme cold. Others say: No, rather it is the most foul stench."

Others said: rather it is the stinking.

Those who said this:

* I was told by al-Musayyab, from Ibrahim al-Nakri, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn Buraida, who said: "Ghassāq: the stinking, and it is in the Tukhariyya dialect." [[Perhaps he means by "al-Tukhariyya" that which is attributed to Tukharistan, with a vowelled first letter, a region of the non-Arab lands east of Jurjan; he means that the word "ghassāq" is not of Arabic origin.]]

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If a bucket of ghassāq were poured out in this world, it would stink the people of this world."

The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: it is what flows from their pus, because that is the more prevalent meaning of al-ghusūq, although the other has a sound aspect.

* *

His words ﴿And other of its kind, pairs﴾

The reciters differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited ﴿wa-ākharu min shaklihi azwāj﴾ in the singular, meaning: this is scalding water and ghassāq, so let them taste it, and another punishment of a similar kind, of various kinds and types, as one says: "for you is punishment from so-and-so: kinds and types." It is possible that by "pairs" is meant the report about the scalding water and ghassāq, and "other of its kind," and that makes three things, so it was said "pairs," meaning that those three things are described as pairs. Some of the Meccans and some of the Basrans recited it as "wa-akharu" in the plural, and it seems that whoever recited it so thought that "azwāj," being the plural of a single attribute, could not be correct, so he made "akhar" plural so that "azwāj" would be an attribute of it; and the Arabs do not forbid describing a noun, when it is an action, with the many, the few, or the two, as we have explained, so one says: "the punishments of so-and-so are kinds, two different kinds."

The recitation I prefer most of the two is to recite ﴿wa-ākharu﴾ in the singular, although the other is correct, since its recitation is widespread among the readers of the metropolitan cities. We chose the singular only because it is sounder in its grammatical derivation in Arabic, and because in interpretation it has the meaning of the singular. It has been said that it is the Zamharir (extreme cold).

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Murra, from Abd Allah, regarding ﴿And other of its kind, pairs﴾, he said: "The Zamharir."

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Murra, from Abd Allah, similarly.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from one who informed him, from Abd Allah, similarly, except that he said: "the punishment of the Zamharir."

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Murra al-Hamdani, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "It is the Zamharir."

* I was told by Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida, from Mubarak ibn Fudala, from al-Hasan, who said: "God mentioned the punishment, mentioning the chains and the shackles, and what exists in this world, then He said: ﴿And other of its kind, pairs﴾." He said: "And other, not seen in this world."

As for His words ﴿of its kind﴾, its meaning is: of its sort. One man says to another: "You are not of my kind" (ma anta min shakli), meaning: you are not of my sort, with the shin vowelled with a fatha. As for "al-shakl," it is from a woman what she adorns herself with of that by which she is made beautiful, and it is also coquetry from her.

And the interpreters said similarly to what we have said.

Those who said this:

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And other of its kind, pairs﴾, he said: "That is: of its like."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿And other of its kind, pairs﴾: "Of its like."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And other of its kind, pairs﴾: "Of every kind is that punishment which God named, pairs which God did not name." He said: "And shakl: the similar."

* *

His words ﴿pairs﴾

That is: kinds and types.

The interpreters said similarly to what we have said.

Those who said this:

* Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And other of its kind, pairs﴾, he said: "Kinds of punishment."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿pairs﴾: "Pair after pair of punishment."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿pairs﴾: "Pairs of punishment in the Fire."

* *

His words ﴿This! A troop rushing in with you﴾

God, may He be remembered, means by His words ﴿This is a troop﴾: this is a group and a company rushing in with you, O transgressors, into the Fire; and that is the entry of one nation of disbelieving nations after another. ﴿No welcome for them! They will burn in the Fire﴾: this is a report from God about the speech of the transgressors who had already entered the Fire before this troop rushing in, saying to the troop entering after them: "No welcome for them!" But the speech is connected so that it becomes as if it were one speech, as it was said: ﴿He wants to drive you out of your land, so what do you advise?﴾ so the words of Pharaoh are connected to the words of his chiefs. This is like what God, may He be remembered, said reporting about the people of the Fire: ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾.

By their words ﴿No welcome for them!﴾ they mean: may their dwellings not be widened for them, as Abu al-Aswad said:

*No welcome to your valley, which is not narrow.* [[This is a half-verse of Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali, mentioned by Abu Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 212 of the Cairo University photocopy no. 26059), who said regarding God's words "No welcome for them!": the Arabs say to a man: "No welcome to you," meaning: may you not be given room, i.e., may you not be widened. Abu al-Aswad said: "No welcome to your valley, which is not narrow." I have not found it in his biography in al-Aghani, nor in Yaqut's dictionary.]]

And the interpreters said similarly to what we have said.

Those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿This is a troop rushing in with you﴾ into the Fire ﴿No welcome for them! They will burn in the Fire. They will say: Rather, you! No welcome for you!﴾ ... up to: ﴿and wretched is the resting place﴾, he said: "These followers say to the leaders."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿This is a troop rushing in with you. No welcome for them!﴾: "The troop: the people who enter in a troop after a troop." And he recited: ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾, the one which was before it.

* *

His words ﴿They will burn in the Fire﴾

He says: they are those who will arrive at the Fire and enter it. ﴿They will say: Rather, you! No welcome for you!﴾: the troop arriving at Hell says to the transgressors whose attributes He, may His praise be exalted, described: "Rather you, O people! No welcome for you," that is: may your places not be widened for you. ﴿You have brought this upon us﴾: they mean: you have brought upon us the dwelling of this place and the burning of the Fire by your misguiding us, and your calling us to disbelieve in God and deny His messengers, until we were led astray by following you, so we deserved the dwelling of Hell today; this is their bringing forward for them what they brought forward in the world of God's punishment for them in the Hereafter. ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾: he says: wretched is the place in which one settles, Hell.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 61:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, add to him a double punishment in the Fire."﴾ (38:61)

This is also the speech of the group that rushes in upon the tyrants, and they were the followers of the tyrants in the world. He, may His praise be exalted, says: The followers said, ﴿"Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us"﴾, meaning: whoever prepared this for them in the world by calling them to the deeds that made the Fire necessary for them, its entry and the dwelling in the abode they dwelt in. By their saying ﴿this﴾ they mean the punishment that we have entered, ﴿"so add to him a double punishment in the Fire"﴾. They say: increase for him the punishment in the Fire upon the punishment he is already in, therein. This too is from the supplication of the followers against those they followed.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention: ﴿And they will say, "What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil?"﴾ [38:62] ﴿Did we take them in mockery, or have our eyes swerved away from them?﴾ [38:63] ﴿Indeed, that is true: the disputing of the people of the Fire.﴾ [38:64]

He, exalted is His mention, says: The tyrants whose description Majestic is His praise has given in these verses said — and they are, as has been related, Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and their kind — ﴿What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men?﴾ meaning: What is wrong with us that we do not see among us in the Fire men ﴿whom we used to count among the evil?﴾ meaning: whom we used to count among our evildoers in the world. By this, as has been related, they meant Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal and Salman.

Those of the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil?﴾, said: That is Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira; and he mentioned people: Suhayb, Ammar and Khabbab, whom we used to count among the evil in the world.

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us: Ibn Idris narrated to us: I heard Layth mention from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And they will say, "What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil?"﴾, he said: They said: Where is Salman? Where is Khabbab? Where is Bilal?

* *

As for His saying ﴿Did we take them in mockery﴾

The readers differed in its recitation. The majority of the readers of Medina and Syria, and some readers of Kufa, recited ﴿atakhadhnahum﴾ with a fath on the alif of "atakhadhnahum" and a cut of it in the form of a question. The majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra, and some readers of Mecca, recited it with a wasl (connected) alif of "ittakhadhnahum". We have already explained earlier that every interrogative that carries the sense of wonder and reproach — the Arabs sometimes use the interrogative form in it and sometimes express it in the form of a statement.

The more correct of the two readings in this matter is the reading of the one who recited it with wasl and not in the form of a question, because the interrogative came before it in His saying ﴿What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil?﴾, so that His saying "ittakhadhnahum" as a statement is preferable, although the interrogative also has a understandable form, for what I described earlier, that it carries the sense of wonder.

Since the correct recitation in this matter is what we have chosen for the reasons we described, the meaning of the speech is: The tyrants said: What is [the matter] with us that we do not see Salman, Bilal and Khabbab, whom we used to count as evil in the world? Did we take them in the world as objects of mockery, whom we ridiculed in it, while they are with us today in the Fire?

Some of the scholars of Arabic from Basra used to say: Whoever pronounces the sin with a kasra in "al-sikhriyy", he means by it "al-huzu'" (ridicule), meaning he mocks them; and whoever pronounces it with a damma, he makes it from "al-sukhra" (servitude), meaning they enslave them, i.e., their eyes swerved away from them while they were with them.

Those of the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Did we take them in mockery, or have our eyes swerved away from them?﴾, he said: Are they in the Fire while we do not know their place?

It was related to me from al-Muharibi, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿And they will say, "What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil?"﴾, he said: They are a people who used to mock Muhammad and his companions. He took them and his companions to Paradise and brought them to the Fire, and they said: ﴿What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil? Did we take them in mockery, or have our eyes swerved away from them?﴾ They say: Our eyes have swerved away from them, so we do not know where they are.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me: Abu Asim narrated to us: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me: al-Hasan narrated to us: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿atakhadhnahum sikhriyyan﴾, he said: We erred regarding them. ﴿Or have our eyes swerved away from them?﴾ — and we do not see them?

Bishr narrated to us: Yazid narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿And they will say, "What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil?"﴾, he said: They lost the people of Paradise. ﴿Did we take them in mockery﴾ in the world, ﴿or have our eyes swerved away from them?﴾ while they are with us in the Fire.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, that is true﴾

Exalted is His mention says: Indeed, this which I have informed you, O people, of the report about the mutual reproach of the people of the Fire, and the cursing of some of them by others, and the calling down of some of them upon others in the Fire, is true and certain. So do not doubt it, but be certain of it: the disputing of the people of the Fire.

* *

As for His saying ﴿the disputing﴾

It is an explanation of His saying ﴿true﴾, and the meaning of the speech is: Indeed, the disputing of the people of the Fire of which I informed you is true.

Some of the scholars of Arabic from Basra used to direct the meaning of His saying ﴿or have our eyes swerved away from them?﴾ to: Rather, our eyes have swerved away from them.

Yunus narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, that is true: the disputing of the people of the Fire﴾, and he recited: ﴿By God, we were indeed in clear error when we made you equal with the Lord of the worlds﴾ [26:97–98], and he recited: ﴿On the Day We gather them all together…﴾ [34:40] until he reached: ﴿Indeed, we were heedless of your worship﴾ [10:29]. He said: If you were worshipping us, as you claim, then "we were heedless of your worship." We did not hear or see. He said: And these are the idols. He said: This is the disputing of the people of the Fire. And he recited: ﴿And what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them﴾ [11:21]. He said: What they used to fabricate in the world has gone astray from them on the Day of Resurrection.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Syria, and some readers of Kufa, recited ﴿atakhadhnahum﴾ with a fath on the alif of "atakhadhnahum" and a cut of it in the form of a question. The majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra, and some readers of Mecca, recited it with a wasl (connected) alif of "ittakhadhnahum". We have already explained earlier that every interrogative that carries the sense of wonder and reproach — the Arabs sometimes use the interrogative form in it and sometimes express it in the form of a statement.

The more correct of the two readings in this matter is the reading of the one who recited it with wasl and not in the form of a question, because the interrogative came before it in His saying ﴿What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil?﴾, so that His saying "ittakhadhnahum" as a statement is preferable, although the interrogative also has a understandable form, for what I described earlier, that it carries the sense of wonder.

Since the correct recitation in this matter is what we have chosen for the reasons we described, the meaning of the speech is: The tyrants said: What is [the matter] with us that we do not see Salman, Bilal and Khabbab, whom we used to count as evil in the world? Did we take them in the world as objects of mockery, whom we ridiculed in it, while they are with us today in the Fire?

Some of the scholars of Arabic from Basra used to say: Whoever pronounces the sin with a kasra in "al-sikhriyy", he means by it "al-huzu'" (ridicule), meaning he mocks them; and whoever pronounces it with a damma, he makes it from "al-sukhra" (servitude), meaning they enslave them, i.e., their eyes swerved away from them while they were with them.

Those of the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Did we take them in mockery, or have our eyes swerved away from them?﴾, he said: Are they in the Fire while we do not know their place?

It was related to me from al-Muharibi, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿And they will say, "What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil?"﴾, he said: They are a people who used to mock Muhammad and his companions. He took them and his companions to Paradise and brought them to the Fire, and they said: ﴿What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil? Did we take them in mockery, or have our eyes swerved away from them?﴾ They say: Our eyes have swerved away from them, so we do not know where they are.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me: Abu Asim narrated to us: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me: al-Hasan narrated to us: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿atakhadhnahum sikhriyyan﴾, he said: We erred regarding them. ﴿Or have our eyes swerved away from them?﴾ — and we do not see them?

Bishr narrated to us: Yazid narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿And they will say, "What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil?"﴾, he said: They lost the people of Paradise. ﴿Did we take them in mockery﴾ in the world, ﴿or have our eyes swerved away from them?﴾ while they are with us in the Fire.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, that is true﴾

Exalted is His mention says: Indeed, this which I have informed you, O people, of the report about the mutual reproach of the people of the Fire, and the cursing of some of them by others, and the calling down of some of them upon others in the Fire, is true and certain. So do not doubt it, but be certain of it: the disputing of the people of the Fire.

* *

As for His saying ﴿the disputing﴾

It is an explanation of His saying ﴿true﴾, and the meaning of the speech is: Indeed, the disputing of the people of the Fire of which I informed you is true.

Some of the scholars of Arabic from Basra used to direct the meaning of His saying ﴿or have our eyes swerved away from them?﴾ to: Rather, our eyes have swerved away from them.

Yunus narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, that is true: the disputing of the people of the Fire﴾, and he recited: ﴿By God, we were indeed in clear error when we made you equal with the Lord of the worlds﴾ [26:97–98], and he recited: ﴿On the Day We gather them all together…﴾ [34:40] until he reached: ﴿Indeed, we were heedless of your worship﴾ [10:29]. He said: If you were worshipping us, as you claim, then "we were heedless of your worship." We did not hear or see. He said: And these are the idols. He said: This is the disputing of the people of the Fire. And he recited: ﴿And what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them﴾ [11:21]. He said: What they used to fabricate in the world has gone astray from them on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 65–66:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "I am only a warner, and there is no god except Allah, the One, the Subduer.[65] Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Mighty, the Forgiving."[66]﴾

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people: ﴿I am only a warner﴾ to you, O assembly of Quraysh, before a severe punishment; I warn you of the punishment and wrath of Allah descending upon you for your disbelief in Him. So beware of it, and hasten to repent before it befalls you. ﴿And there is no god except Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ He means: there is no worshipped one who is fit to be worshipped and deserving of lordship except Allah, to whom everything submits and every creature worships, the One who must not have a partner in His dominion and must not have a consort, the Subduer of everything other than Himself by His power. ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾, He means: the Owner of the heavens and the earth and whatever creation is between them. He means: this One, who has these attributes, is the God besides whom there is no god, not the one who owns nothing and neither harms nor benefits.

* *

As for His saying ﴿the Mighty, the Forgiving﴾:

He means: the Mighty in His vengeance upon the people of disbelief in Him, who claim with Him another god, and the Forgiving of the sins of those among them who repent, and of others, from their disbelief and their disobedience, when they turn back to belief in Him and obedience to Him by abiding by His command and prohibition.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 67–70:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: It is a great news, [67] from which you turn away. [68] I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they disputed. [69] It is only revealed to me that I am a plain warner.﴾ [70]

Exalted is He, mentioning to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to your people who deny what you have brought them from Allah, this Qur'an, and who say to you concerning it: "This is nothing but fabrication": ﴿It is a great news﴾, meaning: this Qur'an is a great report.

And in accordance with what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Those who said that:

* Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil al-Asadi related to me, saying: Abu Usama related to us, from Shibl ibn Abbad, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿Say: It is a great news, from which you turn away﴾, he said: The Qur'an.

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Hisham informed us, from Ibn Sirin, from Shurayh, that a man said to him: "Will you judge against me by the news?" Shurayh said to him: "Is not the Qur'an a news?" He said: and he recited this verse: ﴿Say: It is a great news﴾. He said: and he judged against him.

* Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying ﴿Say: It is a great news, from which you turn away﴾, he said: The Qur'an.

* * *

And His saying ﴿from which you turn away﴾

Meaning: you turn away from it, not acting upon it, and not believing in the proofs and signs of Allah contained within it.

* * *

And His saying ﴿I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly﴾

Saying to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people: ﴿I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they disputed﴾ concerning the matter of Adam, before my Lord revealed to me and informed me of that. Meaning: in my informing you of that there is a clear proof that this Qur'an is a revelation from Allah and a sending down from Him, because you know that knowledge of that was not with me before the descent of this Qur'an, nor is it something I witnessed and observed, but I came to know it through Allah's informing me of it.

And in accordance with what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they disputed﴾, he said: The exalted assembly: the angels, when they consulted about the creation of Adam, and disputed concerning it, and said: "Will You place in it one who causes corruption therein?"

* Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿the exalted assembly when they disputed﴾ is: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed I will make on earth a successive authority"﴾.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying (I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly), he said: They are the angels, their dispute was concerning the matter of Adam when your Lord said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay﴾ ... until ﴿prostrating﴾, and when He said: ﴿Indeed, I will make on earth a successive authority﴾ ... until ﴿and shed blood﴾. In this, the exalted assembly disputed.

* * *

And His saying ﴿It is only revealed to me that I am a plain warner﴾

Exalted is He, saying to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of Quraysh: What is revealed to me is not knowledge of what I have no knowledge of, such as knowledge of the exalted assembly and their dispute over the matter of Adam when He willed to create him, but only because I am a plain warner. So "innama" according to this interpretation is in the genitive position according to the view of those who hold that such a particle as we have mentioned must have a governing particle, so its omission and its presence are equal. As for the view of those who held that such a construction is in the accusative when its governing particle is omitted, then according to his school it is accusative. We have explained this earlier in a way that suffices without repeating it in this place.

There may also be another way to read this statement, namely that its meaning is: "What is revealed to me is for your warning." When the statement is directed to this meaning, "innama" is in the nominative position, because the statement then becomes equivalent to: "What is revealed to me is only the warning."

* * *

His saying ﴿only that I am a plain warner﴾

Meaning: only that I am a warner to you, clearly making you understand, except for your warning. It has been said: "Only that I am" and not "only that you are," and the report is from Muhammad about Allah, because revelation is speech, so it takes the sense of narration, just as one says in speech: "Inform me that I am a wrongdoer" and "Inform me that you are a wrongdoer" with one meaning, as the poet said:

Two men of Dabba informed us
that we saw a man naked.

[This verse is among the evidences of al-Farra' in his Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 282). He said: As for His saying "It is only revealed to me that I am a plain warner": if you wish, make "innama" in the nominative position (substitute subject of yuha) as if you said: "What is revealed to me is only the warning." And if you wish, make the meaning: "What is revealed to me is because I am a prophet and warner." When you drop the lam, the position of "innama" is accusative, and in this position it would be: "What is revealed to me is only that you are a plain warner," because the meaning is narration, as you say in speech: "Inform me that I am a wrongdoer" and "Inform me that you are a wrongdoer." And it is like His saying: "Two men of Dabba... the verse." And the meaning: they two informed us that they saw, and that is permissible because its origin is narration.]

with the meaning: they two informed us that they saw, and that is permissible because the origin of the report is narration.

And His saying ﴿I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly﴾

Saying to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people: ﴿I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they disputed﴾ concerning the matter of Adam, before my Lord revealed to me and informed me of that. Meaning: in my informing you of that there is a clear proof that this Qur'an is a revelation from Allah and a sending down from Him, because you know that knowledge of that was not with me before the descent of this Qur'an, nor is it something I witnessed and observed, but I came to know it through Allah's informing me of it.

And in accordance with what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they disputed﴾, he said: The exalted assembly: the angels, when they consulted about the creation of Adam, and disputed concerning it, and said: "Will You place in it one who causes corruption therein?"

* Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿the exalted assembly when they disputed﴾ is: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed I will make on earth a successive authority"﴾.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying (I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly), he said: They are the angels, their dispute was concerning the matter of Adam when your Lord said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay﴾ ... until ﴿prostrating﴾, and when He said: ﴿Indeed, I will make on earth a successive authority﴾ ... until ﴿and shed blood﴾. In this, the exalted assembly disputed.

* * *

And His saying ﴿It is only revealed to me that I am a plain warner﴾

Exalted is He, saying to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of Quraysh: What is revealed to me is not knowledge of what I have no knowledge of, such as knowledge of the exalted assembly and their dispute over the matter of Adam when He willed to create him, but only because I am a plain warner. So "innama" according to this interpretation is in the genitive position according to the view of those who hold that such a particle as we have mentioned must have a governing particle, so its omission and its presence are equal. As for the view of those who held that such a construction is in the accusative when its governing particle is omitted, then according to his school it is accusative. We have explained this earlier in a way that suffices without repeating it in this place.

There may also be another way to read this statement, namely that its meaning is: "What is revealed to me is for your warning." When the statement is directed to this meaning, "innama" is in the nominative position, because the statement then becomes equivalent to: "What is revealed to me is only the warning."

* * *

His saying ﴿only that I am a plain warner﴾

Meaning: only that I am a warner to you, clearly making you understand, except for your warning. It has been said: "Only that I am" and not "only that you are," and the report is from Muhammad about Allah, because revelation is speech, so it takes the sense of narration, just as one says in speech: "Inform me that I am a wrongdoer" and "Inform me that you are a wrongdoer" with one meaning, as the poet said:

Two men of Dabba informed us
that we saw a man naked.

[This verse is among the evidences of al-Farra' in his Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 282). He said: As for His saying "It is only revealed to me that I am a plain warner": if you wish, make "innama" in the nominative position (substitute subject of yuha) as if you said: "What is revealed to me is only the warning." And if you wish, make the meaning: "What is revealed to me is because I am a prophet and warner." When you drop the lam, the position of "innama" is accusative, and in this position it would be: "What is revealed to me is only that you are a plain warner," because the meaning is narration, as you say in speech: "Inform me that I am a wrongdoer" and "Inform me that you are a wrongdoer." And it is like His saying: "Two men of Dabba... the verse." And the meaning: they two informed us that they saw, and that is permissible because its origin is narration.]

with the meaning: they two informed us that they saw, and that is permissible because the origin of the report is narration.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verses 71–74:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When your Lord said to the angels: "I am going to create a human being from clay. When I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down before him in prostration." So the angels prostrated themselves, all of them together, except Iblis; he was arrogant and became one of the disbelievers.﴾

His saying ﴿When your Lord said﴾

is connected to His saying ﴿when they dispute﴾. The meaning of the speech is: "I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they disputed," at the time when your Lord said, O Muhammad, ﴿to the angels: "I am going to create a human being from clay"﴾, meaning by that the creation of Adam.

* *

His saying ﴿When I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit﴾

The Exalted says: when I have fashioned his creation and made his form proportionate, and breathed into him of My spirit. It has been said: by this is meant, "and breathed into him of My power."

Those who said this:

⁕ I was told, on the authority of al-Musayyib ibn Sharik, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿and breathed into him of My spirit﴾: he said, "of My power."

﴿So fall down before him in prostration﴾ means: prostrate yourselves before him and fall down to him in prostration.

* *

His saying ﴿So the angels prostrated themselves, all of them together﴾

The Exalted says: when God had fashioned that human being, who is Adam, and breathed into him of His spirit, the angels prostrated themselves before him, all of them together, meaning by this the angels who are in the heavens and the earth.

﴿Except Iblis; he was arrogant﴾ means: other than Iblis, for he did not prostrate; he was arrogant about prostrating to him, out of self-exaltation and pride.

(And he became one of the disbelievers) means: and by his self-exaltation and his pride toward his Lord, and his disobedience to His command, he was among those who, in God's foreknowledge, would disbelieve; he denied His lordship and rejected what was incumbent upon him to acknowledge of submission in obedience.

As follows:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr said regarding ﴿Except Iblis; he was arrogant and became one of the disbelievers﴾: he said, Ibn Abbas said, "He was among the disbelievers in God's knowledge."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verses 75–76:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands? Are you arrogant, or were you of the exalted?"﴾ [38:75] ﴿He said, "I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ [38:76]

Exalted is His remembrance says: ﴿He [God]﴾ said to Iblis, when he did not prostrate to Adam and opposed His command: ﴿"O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating"﴾, meaning: what thing prevented you from prostrating ﴿"to what I created with My two hands"﴾, meaning: to the creation of My two hands. In this, He, exalted is His remembrance, informs that He created Adam with His two hands.

As [it is related]:

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd al-Mukattib informed me, saying: I heard Mujahid narrating from Ibn 'Umar, who said: God created four things with His hand: the Throne, Eden, the Pen, and Adam. Then He said to everything, "Be," and it was.

* * *

As for His words ﴿"Are you arrogant"﴾:

He says to Iblis: "Did you magnify yourself above prostrating to Adam, so that you left off prostrating to him out of arrogance toward him, and were not among the arrogant exalted ones before that?" ﴿"Or were you of the exalted?"﴾, meaning: or were you already, before this, one of high station and pride against your Lord? ﴿He said, "I am better than him; You created me from fire"﴾. He, may His praise be majestic, says: Iblis said to his Lord: "I did that, and did not prostrate to the one You commanded me to prostrate to, because I am better than him, and I was better, since You created me from fire and created him from clay, and fire consumes clay and burns it, so fire is better than it." He means: "I did not do that out of arrogance toward You, nor because I was among the exalted, but I did it because I am more noble than him."

This is a rebuke from God to the polytheists who disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ) and refused to submit to him and to follow what came to them from God, out of arrogance at being followers of a man from among them, when they said: ﴿"Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?"﴾ [38:8] and ﴿"This is not but a human like you"﴾ [23:24]. So God, exalted is He, related to them the story of Iblis and his ruin through his arrogance in refusing to prostrate to Adam, by his claim that he was better than him because he was created from fire and Adam was created from clay, until he became an accursed devil, and God's curse and wrath were due upon him. Thereby He warned them that through their arrogance toward Muhammad, their denial of what came to them from God, and their envy and self-magnification, they would deserve the curse and wrath that Iblis deserved by his arrogance in refusing to prostrate to Adam.

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿He said, "Then get out of it, for indeed you are expelled (rajim). And indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense."  He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected."﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying to Iblis: ﴿Then get out of it﴾ means: out of Paradise, ﴿for indeed you are rajim﴾ means: indeed you are stoned (marjum) with the people, reviled and cursed.

As narrated:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿He said, "Then get out of it, for indeed you are rajim"﴾, he said: "Rajim" means accursed.

- I was told on the authority of al-Muharibi, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, with the like of it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And indeed upon you is My curse﴾

It means: and indeed for you is My expulsion from Paradise ﴿until the Day of Recompense﴾, meaning: until the Day of the requital of the servants and their reckoning. ﴿He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected"﴾. His, the Exalted's, saying means: Iblis said to his Lord: "My Lord, since You have cursed me and expelled me from Your Garden," ﴿then reprieve me﴾ means: then delay me in respect of the term, and do not destroy me, ﴿until the Day they are resurrected﴾ means: until the Day when You resurrect Your creatures from their graves.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿He said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all"﴾: He said, "The enemy of God knew that he has no might."

The Interpretation of His, the Exalted, words: ﴿He said, "Then You are among those reprieved, until the Day of the Appointed Time."﴾ ﴿He said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them."﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: God said to Iblis, "Indeed you are among those whom I have reprieved until the Day of the Known Time," which is the time that God made the term of his destruction. I have already explained the time of that in what has passed, according to the differences of the scholars concerning it. He said: ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all﴾: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Iblis said, "By Your might," meaning by Your power, Your authority, and Your dominion over whatever is other than You of Your creation, ﴿I will surely mislead them all﴾, meaning: I will surely lead astray the children of Adam, all of them. ﴿Except Your servants among them, the sincere ones﴾, meaning: except those among them whom You have purified for Your worship and protected from my misguidance, so You have not given me any authority over him, for I am not able to mislead and seduce him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verses 84–86:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿He said: "Then the truth, and the truth I speak"﴾

The readers differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿Then the truth, and the truth I speak﴾. Some of the people of the Hijaz and the majority of the Kufans read the first "al-haqq" with a nominative ending (raf') and the second with an accusative ending (nasb). Regarding the nominative first "al-haqq," when read thus, there are two possibilities. The first is that it is nominative by a pronoun: "God is the truth, and I speak the truth," or "I am the truth and I speak the truth." The second is that it is nominative by implication of His saying ﴿la-amla'anna﴾ (I will surely fill), so the meaning of the speech becomes: "Then the truth is that I will fill Hell with you," just as one says, "A sincere resolve: I will surely come to you," where "resolve" (′azmah) is nominative by implication of "I will surely come to you," since its implication is "that I come to you." As He said: ﴿Then it occurred to them, after they had seen the signs, that they should imprison him﴾ (Yusuf 35), so there must be a nominative subject for His saying ﴿it occurred to them﴾, and it is implied in meaning.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the Meccans and Kufans, read both "al-haqq" with the accusative ending, meaning: "Truly, I will surely fill Hell, and I speak the truth." Then the article "al-" (alif and lam) was attached to it, and it is accusative, because its presence or absence leaves the meaning the same, just as the saying "hamdan lillah" (praise to God) and "al-hamdu lillah" are equivalent to them when it is in the accusative. It is also possible that its accusative form is an imperative of exhortation, meaning: "Hold to the truth, follow the truth." But the first is more fitting, since it is a address from God to Iblis concerning what He will do to him and to his followers.

The most correct of these opinions in my view is to say: they are two widely transmitted readings among the readers of the cities, and whichever of them the reader recites is correct, because both of their meanings are sound.

As for the second "al-haqq," there is no disagreement among all the readers of the cities regarding its accusative ending, meaning: "and I speak the truth."

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Then the truth, and the truth I speak﴾: God says, "I am the Truth, and I speak the truth."

- It was related to me from Ibn Abi Za'idah, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, ﴿Then the truth, and the truth I speak﴾: God says, "The truth is from Me, and I speak the truth."

- Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, he said: al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, he said: Aban ibn Taghlib narrated to us, from Talhah al-Yami, from Mujahid, that he recited it ﴿Fa-al-haqqu﴾ with nominative, ﴿wa-al-haqqa aqulu﴾ with accusative, and said: God says, "I am the Truth, and I speak the truth."

- Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿He said: "Then the truth, and the truth I speak"﴾: he said, "It is an oath which God swore by."

* *

And His saying ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you﴾

He says to Iblis: "I will surely fill Hell with you and with those among the children of Adam who follow you, all of them."

* *

And His saying ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it﴾

Exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people, who say to you ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?﴾ (Sad 8): I do not ask you for any wage, i.e., reward or recompense, for this Reminder, which is the Qur'an that I brought you from God," ﴿and I am not one of those who presume﴾, meaning: "and I am not among those who presume to invent its falsehood and fabrication, so that you would say: ﴿This is nothing but a fabrication he has invented﴾ and ﴿This is nothing but a fabrication.﴾"

As:

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any wage for it, and I am not one of those who presume﴾: "I do not ask you for any wage for the Qur'an, that you give me anything, and I am not among those who presume, inventing and fabricating what God has not commanded me."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 38, verse 87–88:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds﴾ [87] ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time﴾ [88]

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say to these polytheists among your people: ﴿It is not⦆ means: this Qur'an is not ﴿but a reminder⦆ means: nothing but a reminder from Allah ﴿to the worlds⦆ of jinn and humankind, whom their Lord reminds, intending to rescue from destruction those among them who believe in it.

* *

And His words ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time⦆

He says: And you, O polytheists among the Quraysh, will surely know its news, meaning the news of this Qur'an, which is its report, meaning the truth of what it contains of promise and threat, after a time.

Those versed in ta'wil (interpretation) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said so:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And you will surely know its news⦆: "It is the truth of this report; the news of what they denied."  It was said: ﴿its news⦆ is the reality of the matter of Muhammad ﷺ, that he is a Prophet.

Then they differed about the duration of the "time" (hin) mentioned by Allah in this passage: what is it, and what is its endpoint? Some of them said: its endpoint is death.

Mention of those who said so:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time⦆: i.e., after death. And al-Hasan said: "O son of Adam, at death the certain news will come to you."

Others said: its endpoint was the Day of Badr.

Mention of those who said so:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time⦆, he said: "The Day of Badr."

Others said: the Day of Resurrection. And others said: its endpoint is the Resurrection.

Mention of those who said so:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time⦆: "On the Day of Resurrection they will know the news of what they denied, after a time of the world, and that is the Day of Resurrection." And he recited: ﴿For every news there is a fixed time, and you will come to know⦆, and said: "This is also the Hereafter, in which the truth will be established and falsehood will be nullified."

The most correct of these opinions regarding this matter is to say: Allah informed the polytheists who denied this Qur'an that they will know its news after a time, without setting any limit to that time by a fixed boundary. Some of their living people who lived until its truth became manifest and its soundness clear in this world have known it, and some have known the reality of that through their destruction at Badr, and before that. There is no limit among the Arabs for the "time" (hin) that it may not exceed or fall short of. Since this is so, there is no opinion more correct than to leave it unrestricted as Allah left it, without confining it to one time rather than another.

Those versed in ta'wil said the same as those who spoke above.

Mention of those who said so:

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Ikrimah said: "I was asked about a man who swore that he would not do such and such until a time (hin). I said: Indeed, of 'time' there is a time that is not reached, and a time that is reached. The time that is not reached is His words ﴿And you will surely know its news after a time⦆, and the time that is reached is His words ﴿It gives its fruit every time by the permission of its Lord⦆, and that is from the time the date palm is harvested until the time it blossoms, which is six months."

End of the commentary on Surah Sad.
